+        # ``__call__`` (the ASGI factory) doesn't double-mount the endpoint or
+        # re-register the lifespan task.
+        self._wired_app_ids: set[int] = set()
+
+    def _registerable_scopes(self) -> list[str] | None:
+        """The scopes dynamic client registrations may request.
+
+        Returns:
+            The configured ``valid_scopes`` extended with the ``app_scopes`` and
+            ``required_scopes`` names, or None when none are set (any scope
+            accepted). ``required_scopes`` are always registerable: a token has
+            to carry them to pass the endpoint's scope gate, so a client must be
+            allowed to request them -- otherwise required scopes would lock every
+            client out (they could never obtain a token that satisfies the gate).
+        """
+        scopes: list[str] = list(self.valid_scopes or [])
+        for name in (*(self.app_scopes or {}), *(self.required_scopes or [])):
+            if name not in scopes:
+                scopes.append(name)
+        return scopes or None
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Auth-mode resolution.
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _auth_plugin(self) -> Any | None:
+        """Return the configured ``AuthPlugin`` instance, if any.
+
+        Returns:
+            The ``AuthPlugin`` from the active config, or None.
+        """
+        from reflex.config import get_config
+
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.auth import AuthPlugin
+
+        for plugin in get_config().plugins:
+            if isinstance(plugin, AuthPlugin):
+                return plugin
+        return None
+
+    def _auth_enabled(self) -> bool:
+        """Resolve whether MCP OAuth is on for this app.
+
+        When off (no ``AuthPlugin``, or ``auth=False``), the endpoint accepts
+        only anonymous session tokens from the token-granting endpoint --
+        there is no caller-supplied ``token`` model.
+
+        Returns:
+            True when enabled (explicitly, or auto because an ``AuthPlugin``
+            is configured).
+
+        Raises:
+            ConfigError: When ``auth=True`` was forced without an ``AuthPlugin``
+                (the OAuth facade federates login to its providers).
+        """
+        if self.auth is False:
+            return False
+        has_auth_plugin = self._auth_plugin() is not None
+        if self.auth is True and not has_auth_plugin:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "MCPPlugin(auth=True) requires an AuthPlugin in the same config: "
+                "the MCP OAuth flow signs users in through the AuthPlugin's OIDC "
+                "providers. Add rxe.AuthPlugin(...) to plugins, or drop auth=True."
+            )
+        return has_auth_plugin
+
+    def _anonymous_enabled(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the anonymous token endpoint is wired for this plugin.
+
+        Always True when OAuth is off -- the endpoint would otherwise be
+        unreachable (the caller-supplied token model no longer exists).
+
+        Returns:
+            True when anonymous session grants are available.
+        """
+        return self.anonymous_sessions or not self._auth_enabled()
+
+    def _check_requirements(self, app: App) -> bool:
+        """Check that the app meets the requirements for this plugin.
+
+        Args:
+            app: The app instance.
+
+        Returns:
+            True if requirements are met, False otherwise.
+
+        Raises:
+            RuntimeError: If the app is not an AppEnterprise instance.
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.app import AppEnterprise
+
+        if not isinstance(app, AppEnterprise):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "MCPPlugin requires the app to be a "
+                "reflex_enterprise.App (AppEnterprise) instance. "
+                "Update your rxconfig.py to use:\n\n"
+                "  import reflex_enterprise as rxe\n"
+                "  config = rxe.Config(\n"
+                "      app_name='my_app',\n"
+                "      plugins=[rxe.MCPPlugin()],\n"
+                "  )\n\n"
+                "  app = rxe.App()\n"
+            )
+
+        return True
+
+    def _load_fastmcp(self) -> type | None:
+        """Import and return the ``FastMCP`` class, or None if mcp is missing.
+
+        Returns:
+            The ``FastMCP`` class, or None when the ``mcp`` extra is not
+            installed (an actionable error is logged in that case).
+        """
+        try:
+            from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
+        except ImportError:
+            # Escape so rich (used by console.error) renders the `[mcp]` extra
+            # literally instead of parsing it as a `[mcp]` markup tag.
+            console.error(rich.markup.escape(_MISSING_MCP_DEPS_MESSAGE))
+            return None
+        return FastMCP
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _mcp_available() -> bool:
+        """Whether the optional ``mcp`` SDK is importable, without logging.
+
+        ``register_routes`` (which runs before ``post_compile``) uses this to
+        avoid registering an orphan consent page when the MCP server itself
+        will not be built. ``post_compile`` logs the actionable missing-deps
+        error via :meth:`_load_fastmcp`, so this stays quiet to avoid emitting
+        it twice.
+
+        Returns:
+            True when ``mcp.server.fastmcp`` can be located.
+        """
+        import importlib.util
+
+        try:
+            return importlib.util.find_spec("mcp.server.fastmcp") is not None
+        except ModuleNotFoundError:
+            return False
+
+    def get_mcp_server(self) -> Any:
+        """Return this plugin's built ``FastMCP`` server instance.
+
+        Returns:
+            The ``FastMCP`` instance.
+
+        Raises:
+            RuntimeError: If the server has not been built yet (the app has not
+                been compiled, or the ``mcp`` extra is missing).
+        """
+        if self._mcp_server is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "MCPPlugin has not built its server yet -- it is created when "
+                "the app is compiled. Access it after compile (e.g. in a reflex "
+                "lifespan task) or via MCPPlugin(configure=...)."
+            )
+        return self._mcp_server
+
+    def _run_configure(self, mcp_server: Any) -> None:
+        """Invoke the ``configure`` hook with the built server, if provided.
+
+        Args:
+            mcp_server: The built ``FastMCP`` instance.
+        """
+        if self.configure is None:
+            return
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.auth import _resolve_import_path
+
+        fn = (
+            _resolve_import_path(self.configure)
+            if isinstance(self.configure, str)
+            else self.configure
+        )
+        fn(mcp_server)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Route registration (called by AppEnterprise at construction).
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def register_routes(self, app: Any) -> None:
+        """Register the consent page before the compiler snapshots pages.
+
+        Only applies when MCP OAuth is enabled. The page is registered with
+        ``auth=True`` so the page guard federates an anonymous visitor through
+        the ``AuthPlugin`` login flow (any configured provider) and back to the
+        consent prompt.
+
+        Args:
+            app: The app to add the page to.
+        """
+        if not self._auth_enabled():
+            return
+        # The consent page only functions once ``post_compile`` wires the OAuth
+        # server, which it skips (with an actionable error) when the optional
+        # ``mcp`` extra is missing. Skip registering an orphan, non-functional
+        # consent page in that case so the app stays coherent -- no MCP surface
+        # at all without the extra, rather than a dead page whose on_load has no
+        # bound authorization server to resolve.
+        if not self._mcp_available():
+            return
+        # Reject only a consent path that is the mount itself or genuinely
+        # nested under it (segment boundary), not a mere string-prefix sibling
+        # like path=/mcp + consent_path=/mcp-consent-page.
+        mount = self.path.rstrip("/")
+        if self.consent_path == mount or self.consent_path.startswith(mount + "/"):
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"MCPPlugin consent_path {self.consent_path!r} must not live "
+                f"under the MCP mount path {self.path!r}: the backend owns that "
+                "mount, so the consent page would be unreachable."
+            )
+
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement import reserve_agent_hidden_route
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.consent_state import MCPConsentState
+
+        app.add_page(
+            self._consent_page_component(),
+            route=self.consent_path,
+            auth=True,
+            on_load=MCPConsentState.load_authorization_request,
+            title="Authorize MCP access",
+        )
+        # The consent page is human-interactive auth plumbing; keep it out of the
+        # agent-facing page listing (MCP instructions / EventHandlerAPI OpenAPI).
+        reserve_agent_hidden_route(app, self.consent_path)
+
+    def _consent_page_component(self) -> Any:
+        """Wrap the consent page builder into the callable ``add_page`` expects.
+
+        Returns:
+            A zero-argument callable returning the page component.
+        """
+
+        def page() -> Any:
+            from reflex_enterprise.plugins.auth import _resolve_import_path
+            from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.pages import default_consent_page
+
+            spec = self.consent_page
+            fn = (
+                default_consent_page
+                if spec is None
+                else _resolve_import_path(spec)
+                if isinstance(spec, str)
+                else spec
+            )
+            return fn(plugin=self)
+
+        # Surface a meaningful name in duplicate-route errors.
+        page.__name__ = page.__qualname__ = "default_consent_page"
+        return page
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Server info / instructions.
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _build_server_info(
+        self,
+        app: App,
+        descriptions: list[dict[str, Any]],
+        *,
+        auth_enabled: bool = False,
+        anonymous_enabled: bool = True,
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Build the general server-info payload that backs ``instructions``.
+
+        This is the MCP analog of the OpenAPI spec's ``info`` preamble: it says
+        what the server is, where the app is served, how to authenticate, how
+        the tools fit together, and which pages / dynamic route variables exist.
+        :meth:`_build_instructions` renders it into the server ``instructions``
+        shown to clients on connect.
+
+        Args:
+            app: The reflex app.
+            descriptions: The snapshotted handler descriptions.
+            auth_enabled: Whether the OAuth authorization flow is active.
+            anonymous_enabled: Whether the anonymous token endpoint is wired.
+
+        Returns:
+            A JSON-serialisable server-info dict.
+        """
+        from reflex.config import get_config
+        from reflex.state import State
+
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.api_tokens import TOKEN_ENDPOINT_PATH
+
+        config = get_config()
+        pages, dynamic_route_args = collect_page_info(app)
+        # Fully-qualified names of the states an agent is likely to read, for the
+        # `reflex://state/vars` resource: the root (whole app state) plus every
+        # state that owns a public handler. Any valid state name works, not just
+        # these.
+        state_names = sorted(
+            {State.get_full_name()}
+            | {
+                reh.handler.state.get_full_name()
+                for reh in iter_public_event_handlers()
+                if reh.handler.state is not None
+            }
+        )
+        # User-defined ``rxe.mcp.resource`` methods, surfaced so agents can read
+        # them directly (they are also discoverable via resources/templates/list).
+        from reflex_enterprise.mcp import (
+            iter_state_resources,
+            resource_parameter_names,
+            resource_uri_template,
+        )
+
+        var_resources: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+        for res_state, res_method, res_fn, res_spec in iter_state_resources():
+            res_doc = inspect.getdoc(res_fn)
+            var_resources.append(
+                {
+                    "uri": resource_uri_template(
+                        res_state,
+                        res_method,
+                        resource_parameter_names(res_fn),
+                    ),
+                    "summary": res_spec.description
+                    or (res_doc.splitlines()[0].strip() if res_doc else res_method),
+                }
+            )
+        # Every request requires an app-issued bearer token; the tools operate
+        # on the session bound to it (there is never a token argument).
+        anonymous_hint = (
+            "For an anonymous session (no user identity; only public surfaces "
+            "when the app enforces auth), POST to the app's token endpoint "
+            f"`{TOKEN_ENDPOINT_PATH}` and use the returned `access_token` as "
+            "your Bearer token."
+        )
+        if auth_enabled:
+            description = (
+                "Requests require an OAuth 2.1 Bearer token issued by this "
+                "app. Discovery is standard MCP authorization: an "
+                "unauthenticated request gets a 401 whose WWW-Authenticate "
+                "header points at the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata; "
+                "register via dynamic client registration and complete the "
+                "browser-based login/consent flow. Tools operate on the "
+                "session bound to your token -- there is no token argument."
+            )
+            if anonymous_enabled:
+                description += " " + anonymous_hint
+            authentication: dict[str, Any] = {
+                "type": "oauth2",
+                "description": description,
+            }
+        else:
+            authentication = {
+                "type": "bearer",
+                "description": (
+                    "Requests require an app-issued Bearer token. "
+                    + anonymous_hint
+                    + " The session is server-generated and bound to the "
+                    "token; reuse the token across calls to address the same "
+                    "session."
+                ),
+            }
+        tools: dict[str, str] = {}
+        if self.expose_events:
+            tools["search_events"] = (
+                "Search the app's event handlers; returns each handler's "
+                "name (for queue_event) and payload schema."
+            )
+            tools["queue_event"] = (
+                "Apply an event to your session: event_name + payload (the "
+                "handler's parameters) + optional query (a JSON object of "
+                "query parameters, e.g. the dynamic route variables listed "
+                "below). Returns the resulting state delta -- or, for a "
+                "file-upload handler, out-of-band upload directions (files "
+                "must be POSTed to the MCP upload endpoint separately)."
+            )
+        # State (+ event, when exposed) introspection over the ``reflex://``
+        # resource family; the session always rides the bearer.
+        resources = ["`reflex://state` -- list the exposed state names."]
+        if self.expose_events:
+            resources += [
+                "`reflex://event` -- enumerate the event handlers; "
+                "`reflex://event/<event_name>` -- one handler's full schema.",
+                "`reflex://state/events/<state_name>` -- the event handlers on a state.",
+            ]
+        resources += [
+            "`reflex://state/vars/<state_name>` -- the resolved "
+            "`.dict()` rooted at a state (cached frontend + computed var values); "
+            "read the root `reflex___state____state` for the whole app.",
+            "`reflex://state/vars/<state_name>/<var_name>` -- a single "
+            "var's live value (a computed var is marked dirty and recomputed).",
+        ]
+        if self.expose_events:
+            workflow = (
+                "Call search_events (or read `reflex://event`) to find an event "
+                "and its payload schema, queue_event to apply it to your "
+                "session, then read `reflex://state/vars/<state_name>` to "
+                "inspect the resulting state."
+            )
+        else:
+            workflow = (
+                "This server exposes read access to session state (plus any "
+                "app-defined tools/resources); the app's event handlers are "
+                "not exposed. Read `reflex://state/vars/<state_name>` to "
+                "inspect state."
+            )
+        if self.pending_updates == "queue":
+            tools["get_pending_updates"] = (
+                "Return and clear followup deltas buffered for the session "
+                "(chained events, background-task results)."
+            )
+        info: dict[str, Any] = {
+            "name": self.server_name or f"{config.app_name} MCP",
+            "app_name": config.app_name,
+            "version": self.api_version,
+            # Where the app itself is served (None if not configured).
+            "server_url": resolve_server_url(config),
+            "mcp_endpoint": self.path,
+            "authentication": authentication,
+            "tools": tools,
+            "resources": resources,
+            "state_resources": state_names,
+            "var_resources": var_resources,
+            "workflow": workflow,
+            "event_handler_count": len(descriptions),
+            "expose_events": self.expose_events,
+            "pages": pages,
+            "dynamic_route_variables": sorted(dynamic_route_args),
+        }
+        if self.contact:
+            info["contact"] = self.contact
+        if self.license_info:
+            info["license"] = self.license_info
+        return info
+
+    def _build_instructions(self, server_info: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+        """Render the server-info payload as an MCP ``instructions`` string.
+
+        Args:
+            server_info: The payload from :meth:`_build_server_info`.
+
+        Returns:
+            A markdown description shown to connecting MCP clients.
+        """
+        exposes_events = bool(server_info.get("expose_events", True))
+        tool_lines: list[str] = []
+        if "search_events" in server_info["tools"]:
+            tool_lines.append(
+                f"- `search_events(query)` -- {server_info['tools']['search_events']}"
+            )
+        if "queue_event" in server_info["tools"]:
+            tool_lines.append(
+                "- `queue_event(event_name, payload, query)` -- "
+                f"{server_info['tools']['queue_event']}"
+            )
+        if "get_pending_updates" in server_info["tools"]:
+            tool_lines.append(
+                "- `get_pending_updates()` -- "
+                f"{server_info['tools']['get_pending_updates']}"
+            )
+        lines = [
+            f"# {server_info['name']} (v{server_info['version']})",
+            "",
+            f"MCP access to the Reflex app **{server_info['app_name']}**"
+            + (
+                f" and its {server_info['event_handler_count']} event handler(s)."
+                if exposes_events
+                else " (state read access; event handlers are not exposed)."
+            ),
+        ]
+        if server_info["server_url"]:
+            lines += ["", f"The app is served at {server_info['server_url']}."]
+        lines += [
+            "",
+            "## Authentication",
+            "",
+            server_info["authentication"]["description"],
+        ]
+        if tool_lines:
+            lines += ["", "## Tools", "", *tool_lines]
+        lines += [
+            "",
+            "## Resources",
+            "",
+            "Introspect and read the app over `reflex://` resources:",
+            "",
+            *(f"- {line}" for line in server_info["resources"]),
+            "",
+            "Exposed states (for the `<state_name>` above):",
+            "",
+            *(f"- `{name}`" for name in server_info["state_resources"]),
+            "",
+            server_info["workflow"],
+        ]
+        if server_info.get("var_resources"):
+            lines += [
+                "",
+                "## App resources",
+                "",
+                "App-defined, read-only resources returning a value from your "
+                "session state. Each parameter is a required URI path segment.",
+                "",
+                *(
+                    f"- `{res['uri']}`"
+                    + (f" -- {res['summary']}" if res["summary"] else "")
+                    for res in server_info["var_resources"]
+                ),
+            ]
+        if server_info["pages"]:
+            lines += ["", "## Pages", ""]
+            for page in server_info["pages"]:
+                if page["on_load"]:
+                    triggers = ", ".join(f"`{ol['event']}`" for ol in page["on_load"])
+                    lines.append(f"- `{page['url']}` -- on_load triggers {triggers}")
+                else:
+                    lines.append(f"- `{page['url']}`")
+        if server_info["dynamic_route_variables"] and exposes_events:
+            lines += [
+                "",
+                "## Dynamic route variables",
+                "",
+                "These are the query parameters the app's pages declare (from "
+                "their URL patterns). Pass any of them to `queue_event` in the "
+                "`query` object; they reach handlers via `self.router.page.params`, "
+                "exactly as a page URL's query string would.",
+                "",
+                *(f"- `{name}`" for name in server_info["dynamic_route_variables"]),
+            ]
+        if server_info.get("contact"):
+            contact = server_info["contact"]
+            detail = " ".join(
+                part for part in (contact.get("name"), contact.get("email")) if part
+            )
+            lines += ["", "## Contact", "", detail or str(contact)]
+        if server_info.get("license"):
+            license_info = server_info["license"]
+            label = license_info.get("name", "")
+            if license_info.get("url"):
+                label = f"{label} ({license_info['url']})".strip()
+            lines += ["", "## License", "", label]
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # OAuth wiring.
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _resolve_issuer_url(self) -> str:
+        """Resolve the public origin serving the OAuth endpoints.
+
+        Returns:
+            The issuer origin (no trailing slash).
+
+        Raises:
+            ConfigError: When no origin can be determined.
+        """
+        from reflex.config import get_config
+
+        issuer = self.issuer_url or resolve_server_url(get_config())
+        if not issuer:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "MCP OAuth needs the app's public origin for the RFC 8414 "
+                "issuer, but neither MCPPlugin(issuer_url=...) nor the config's "
+                "deploy_url/api_url is set. Configure one of them."
+            )
+        return issuer.rstrip("/")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_issuer_security(issuer_url: str) -> None:
+        """Reject a plain-http OAuth issuer at wiring time.
+
+        The internal OAuth server hands out bearer credentials on this origin;
+        over plain HTTP they (and the authorization codes) are exposed to any
+        on-path observer, so a non-``https`` issuer is a deployment error.
+        Loopback hosts are exempt for development (matching the RFC 8252
+        loopback exception used for redirect URIs).
+
+        Args:
+            issuer_url: The resolved issuer origin.
+
+        Raises:
+            ConfigError: When the issuer is ``http`` on a non-loopback host.
+        """
+        from urllib.parse import urlparse
+
+        parsed = urlparse(issuer_url)
+        if parsed.scheme == "https":
+            return
+        hostname = (parsed.hostname or "").lower()
+        if parsed.scheme == "http" and hostname in _LOOPBACK_ISSUER_HOSTS:
+            return
+        raise ConfigError(
+            f"MCP OAuth issuer {issuer_url!r} must be served over https: the "
+            "authorization server issues bearer credentials on this origin, "
+            "which plain HTTP would expose to any on-path observer. Terminate "
+            "TLS in front of the app and set MCPPlugin(issuer_url=...) (or "
+            "deploy_url/api_url) to the https origin. Plain http is allowed "
+            "only on a loopback host (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) for "
+            "development."
+        )
+
+    def _resolve_consent_url(self, issuer_url: str) -> str:
+        """Resolve the absolute URL of the consent page.
+
+        The consent page is a frontend page, so it lives at the frontend origin
+        (``deploy_url``) -- which differs from the backend issuer origin in
+        split dev deployments.
+
+        Args:
+            issuer_url: The resolved issuer origin (the fallback).
+
+        Returns:
+            The absolute consent page URL.
+        """
+        from reflex.config import get_config
+
+        config = get_config()
+        base = (config.deploy_url or issuer_url).rstrip("/")
+        return base + config.prepend_frontend_path(self.consent_path)
+
+    def _build_auth_store(self) -> MCPAuthStore:
+        """Build (or return the configured) token/consent store.
+
+        Returns:
+            The configured ``auth_store``, a Redis store when the app is
+            configured for Redis, else an in-memory store.
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.store import (
+            InMemoryMCPAuthStore,
+            RedisMCPAuthStore,
+        )
+
+        if self.auth_store is not None:
+            return self.auth_store
+        from reflex.utils.prerequisites import get_redis
+
+        redis = get_redis()
+        if redis is not None:
+            return RedisMCPAuthStore(redis)
+        console.debug(
+            "MCPPlugin: using the in-memory OAuth store (no Redis configured). "
+            "Tokens do not survive restarts and are per-process; configure "
+            "redis_url for multi-worker deployments."
+        )
+        return InMemoryMCPAuthStore()
+
+    def _build_authorization_server(self, app: App) -> MCPAuthorizationServer:
+        """Build and bind the OAuth authorization server for this app.
+
+        Args:
+            app: The reflex app whose sessions tokens bind to.
+
+        Returns:
+            The bound ``MCPAuthorizationServer``.
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.provider import (
+            MCPAuthConfig,
+            MCPAuthorizationServer,
+            bind_mcp_authorization_server,
+        )
+
+        issuer_url = self._resolve_issuer_url()
+        self._validate_issuer_security(issuer_url)
+        config = MCPAuthConfig(
+            issuer_url=issuer_url,
+            resource_server_url=issuer_url + self.path,
+            consent_url=self._resolve_consent_url(issuer_url),
+            pending_authorization_ttl=self.pending_authorization_ttl,
+            authorization_code_ttl=self.authorization_code_ttl,
+            access_token_ttl=self.access_token_ttl,
+            refresh_token_ttl=self.refresh_token_ttl,
+            client_ttl=self.client_registration_ttl,
+            upload_ticket_ttl=self.upload_ticket_ttl,
+            app_scopes=dict(self.app_scopes) if self.app_scopes else None,
+        )
+        server = MCPAuthorizationServer(
+            app=app, store=self._build_auth_store(), config=config
+        )
+        # The consent page's event handlers resolve the server through this
+        # process-wide binding (mirrors enforcement.bind_auth_plugin).
+        bind_mcp_authorization_server(server)
+        return server
+
+    def _register_root_oauth_routes(
+        self, app: App, authorization_server: MCPAuthorizationServer
+    ) -> None:
+        """Serve the AS endpoints + discovery documents at the app root.
+
+        FastMCP registers its own copies *inside* the mounted sub-app, which
+        puts them at ``/_reflex/mcp/...`` -- but RFC 8414 / RFC 9728 discovery
+        looks at the origin root (``/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server``
+        and the path-aware
+        ``/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/_reflex/mcp``). Running FastMCP
+        in resource-server mode (token verifier only) keeps the sub-app free of
+        misplaced AS routes, and the canonical documents/endpoints are
+        registered here, front-inserted so they beat the SPA/proxy catch-all
+        (same trick as the cookie-sync route).
+
+        Args:
+            app: The app whose root router receives the routes.
+            authorization_server: The provider backing the endpoints.
+        """
+        from mcp.server.auth.routes import (
+            create_auth_routes,
+            create_protected_resource_routes,
+        )
+        from mcp.server.auth.settings import (
+            ClientRegistrationOptions,
+            RevocationOptions,
+        )
+        from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl
+        from starlette.routing import Route
+
+        config = authorization_server.config
+        registerable_scopes = self._registerable_scopes()
+
+        # The OAuth endpoint paths, each front-inserted at the origin root. Maps
+        # the SDK's module constant -> the configured path.
+        oauth_paths = {
+            "AUTHORIZATION_PATH": ("authorization_path", self.authorization_path),
+            "TOKEN_PATH": ("token_path", self.token_path),
+            "REGISTRATION_PATH": ("registration_path", self.registration_path),
+            "REVOCATION_PATH": ("revocation_path", self.revocation_path),
+        }
+
+        # Reject a path nested under the MCP mount (the backend owns that mount as
+        # a prefix, so a route there is shadowed and would 404). Mirrors the
+        # consent-path guard.
+        mount = self.path.rstrip("/")
+        for label, oauth_path in oauth_paths.values():
+            if oauth_path == mount or oauth_path.startswith(mount + "/"):
+                raise ConfigError(
+                    f"MCPPlugin {label} {oauth_path!r} must not live under the MCP "
+                    f"mount path {self.path!r}: the mounted MCP sub-app would "
+                    "shadow it, so that endpoint would 404."
+                )
+        # Distinct paths, else two endpoints collide on one route (and the
+        # metadata advertises the same URL for both).
+        chosen = [path for _, path in oauth_paths.values()]
+        if len(set(chosen)) != len(chosen):
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "MCPPlugin authorization_path / token_path / registration_path / "
+                f"revocation_path must be distinct, got {sorted(chosen)}."
+            )
+
+        # The SDK hardcodes each endpoint path as a module constant -- used for
+        # both the route and the advertised metadata endpoint -- with no override
+        # parameter. ``/register`` in particular is a common app sign-up path.
+        # Scope overrides around the single build call so every route AND its
+        # advertised endpoint stay consistent, then restore them immediately
+        # (this runs once, single-threaded, at app compile).
+        import mcp.server.auth.routes as _sdk_auth_routes
+
+        _saved_paths = {
+            const: getattr(_sdk_auth_routes, const) for const in oauth_paths
+        }
+        for const, (_, value) in oauth_paths.items():
+            setattr(_sdk_auth_routes, const, value)
+        try:
+            as_routes = create_auth_routes(
+                provider=authorization_server,
+                issuer_url=AnyHttpUrl(config.issuer_url),
+                client_registration_options=ClientRegistrationOptions(
+                    enabled=self.enable_dynamic_client_registration,
+                    valid_scopes=registerable_scopes,
+                    default_scopes=self.default_scopes,
+                    # Advertise the same expiry the store enforces, so a
+                    # confidential client learns its secret's
+                    # ``client_secret_expires_at`` instead of being told it never
+                    # expires and later failing with ``invalid_client`` once the
+                    # registration is swept. ``None`` (registrations kept forever)
+                    # advertises "no expiry" to match.
+                    client_secret_expiry_seconds=(
+                        int(self.client_registration_ttl)
+                        if self.client_registration_ttl is not None
+                        else None
+                    ),
+                ),
+                revocation_options=RevocationOptions(
+                    enabled=self.enable_token_revocation
+                ),
+            )
+        finally:
+            for const, value in _saved_paths.items():
+                setattr(_sdk_auth_routes, const, value)
+        if self.registration_rate_limit > 0:
+            as_routes = [
+                Route(
+                    route.path,
+                    endpoint=_RegistrationRateLimiter(
+                        route.app,
+                        limit=self.registration_rate_limit,
+                        window=self.registration_rate_window,
+                        trusted_proxy_hops=self.registration_trusted_proxy_hops,
+                    ),
+                    methods=["POST", "OPTIONS"],
+                )
+                if route.path == self.registration_path
+                else route
+                for route in as_routes
+            ]
+        prm_routes = create_protected_resource_routes(
+            resource_url=AnyHttpUrl(config.resource_server_url),
+            authorization_servers=[AnyHttpUrl(config.issuer_url)],
+            # ``_registerable_scopes`` already folds in ``required_scopes``, so
+            # this advertises them in the resource metadata too.
+            scopes_supported=registerable_scopes,
+        )
+        api = app._api
+        assert api is not None  # post_compile guards app._api before calling this
+        # Fail fast on a second OAuth-enabled MCP mount. The facade binds ONE
+        # authorization server per process (``bind_mcp_authorization_server``)
+        # and serves its RFC 8414 discovery document at a fixed, non-mount-scoped
+        # origin path, so a second mount would clobber the binding and shadow the
+        # first mount's endpoints -- a silent, confusing breakage. The AS-metadata
+        # route is owned solely by this facade (the AuthPlugin is an OIDC client,
+        # not an AS), so its prior presence is an unambiguous signal.
+        if any(getattr(r, "path", None) == _AS_METADATA_PATH for r in api.routes):
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "A second OAuth-enabled MCPPlugin is being mounted on this app, "
+                "but only one is supported: the MCP OAuth facade binds a single "
+                "authorization server per process and serves its RFC 8414/9728 "
+                "discovery documents at fixed origin-root paths, so a second "
+                "mount would shadow the first. Mount one MCPPlugin with auth "
+                "enabled; run any additional MCP surfaces with auth=False "
+                "(anonymous sessions)."

+            api.routes.insert(0, route)

+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Compile hook.
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def post_compile(self, **context: Any) -> None:
+        """Build and mount the MCP server after compilation.
+
+        Args:
+            **context: The post-compile context containing the app.
+        """
+        app: App | None = context.get("app")
+        if app is None:
+            return
+
+        if not self._check_requirements(app):
+            return

+        if not app._api:
+            return

+        # duplicate (and the latter raises once the lifespan has started).
+        if id(app) in self._wired_app_ids:

+        anonymous_enabled = self._anonymous_enabled()

+        # the context at request time (when it is not set).
+        handler_index = build_event_handler_index()

+            describe_event_handler(reh) for reh in iter_public_event_handlers()

+            app,
+            descriptions,
+            auth_enabled=auth_enabled,
+            anonymous_enabled=anonymous_enabled,
+        )
+        instructions = self.instructions or self._build_instructions(server_info)

+        # by the tool -- so divert their followup socket emissions (chained
+        # events, background-task results, per-event auth bookkeeping) off the
+        # socket path via this sink instead of logging "disconnected client" for
+        # every one. Sessions register on grant (the anonymous issuer) or seed
+        # (the OAuth exchange), and re-register on use. The guard wraps
+        # emit_update once per app: when a namespace is already guarded (e.g. a

+        # so every server registers tokens on the one sink the guard consults.

+        sink = install_backend_delta_sink(app, BackendDeltaSink()) or BackendDeltaSink()

+            # through the upload path (M10).
+            allowed_upload_handlers = {
+                full_event_handler_name(reh)
+                for reh in iter_public_event_handlers()

+                0,
+                Route(
+                    self.path + "/upload",
+                    endpoint=_MCPUploadEndpoint(
+                        app,

+                    ),
+                    methods=["POST"],
+                ),
+            )
+
+        mcp_server = self._build_server(
+            app,
+            fast_mcp_cls,
+            handler_index,
+            descriptions,
+            server_info["name"],
+            instructions,
+            sink,
+            authorization_server=authorization_server,
+            anonymous_issuer=anonymous_issuer,
+        )
+
+        # Publish the built server for customization: the ``configure`` hook (at
+        # build time, before mounting) and ``get_mcp_server()`` (at runtime). Run
+        # ``configure`` now so any custom tools/resources/prompts are registered
+        # before the transport starts serving.
+        self._mcp_server = mcp_server
+        bind_mcp_server(mcp_server)
+        self._run_configure(mcp_server)
+
+        # ``streamable_http_app()`` lazily creates the session manager and
+        # returns the ASGI sub-app we mount. Nested lifespans on a mounted
+        # sub-app are NOT invoked by Starlette, so the session manager is run

+        @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
+        async def _mcp_session_manager_lifespan(app: App):

+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Server + tools.

+    def _build_server(
+        self,
+        app: App,
+        fast_mcp_cls: type,
+        handler_index: dict[str, RegisteredEventHandler],
+        descriptions: list[dict[str, Any]],
+        server_name: str,
+        instructions: str,
+        sink: BackendDeltaSink,

+        anonymous_issuer: Any = None,
+    ) -> Any:

+
+        The transport always runs in resource-server mode: FastMCP wraps it in
+        ``RequireAuthMiddleware`` and every request must carry an app-issued
+        bearer token -- an OAuth token (when the authorization server is
+        wired), or an anonymous session token from the token-granting
+        endpoint. There is no caller-supplied ``token`` model.
+
+        Args:
+            app: The reflex app the tools operate on.
+            fast_mcp_cls: The ``FastMCP`` class (imported lazily).
+            handler_index: Alias -> handler map for resolving event names.
+            descriptions: Handler descriptions used by the search tool.
+            server_name: The name advertised by the MCP server.
+            instructions: The MCP ``instructions`` shown to connecting clients.
+            sink: The backend-delta sink diverting followup emissions for the
+                browserless MCP session tokens.
+            authorization_server: The OAuth AS, when MCP OAuth is enabled.
+            anonymous_issuer: The anonymous session issuer, when the token
+                endpoint is enabled.

+

+        from mcp.server.auth.settings import AuthSettings
+        from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings
+        from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl
+        from reflex.utils.format import json_dumps
+
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.provider import ReflexMCPTokenVerifier
+
+        if authorization_server is None and anonymous_issuer is None:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "MCPPlugin has no token authority to verify bearers against: "
+                "enable anonymous_sessions or configure an AuthPlugin for the "
+                "OAuth flow."
+            )
+
+        if authorization_server is not None:
+            issuer_url = authorization_server.config.issuer_url
+            resource_server_url = authorization_server.config.resource_server_url
+        else:
+            issuer_url = self._resolve_issuer_url()
+            resource_server_url = issuer_url + self.path
+
+        server_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
+            # FastMCP auto-enables DNS-rebinding protection (a localhost-only
+            # Host allowlist) keyed on its *standalone-serve* host setting,
+            # which is never used here: the transport is mounted inside the
+            # reflex ASGI app and served at whatever public host the app runs
+            # on -- the allowlist would 421 every real deployment. Rebinding
+            # is not a live threat for this endpoint: every request requires an
+            # app-issued bearer token no attacker page holds.
+            "transport_security": TransportSecuritySettings(
+                enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False
+            ),
+            # Resource-server mode: FastMCP wraps the transport in
+            # RequireAuthMiddleware (401 + WWW-Authenticate pointing at the
+            # *root* PRM URL derived from resource_server_url) and does NOT
+            # register AS routes inside the sub-app -- those live at the app
+            # root (see _register_root_oauth_routes) when OAuth is on. The
+            # verifier accepts OAuth tokens and/or anonymous session tokens.
+            "token_verifier": ReflexMCPTokenVerifier(
+                authorization_server, anonymous_issuer=anonymous_issuer
+            ),
+            "auth": AuthSettings(
+                issuer_url=AnyHttpUrl(issuer_url),
+                resource_server_url=AnyHttpUrl(resource_server_url),
+                required_scopes=self.required_scopes,
+            ),
+        }
+
+        # Absolute URL of the MCP upload endpoint (``self.path + "/upload"``)
+        # that file-upload directions point the agent at: agents never hold
+        # the session token, so uploads ride a pre-signed ticket and the
+        # endpoint injects the session token server-side. Built from the
+        # advertised resource origin, which may differ from api_url/deploy_url
+        # when the app sits behind a reverse proxy (configured via issuer_url).
+        mcp_upload_url = resource_server_url.rstrip("/") + "/upload"
+
+        # ``stateless_http`` keeps each tool call independent (session state is
+        # keyed by the bearer token's session -- not the MCP connection);
+        # ``json_response`` returns plain JSON rather than an SSE stream.
+        # The endpoint route lives at ``/`` inside the sub-app, so mounting it at
+        # ``self.path`` serves the whole server from that single path.
+        mcp_server = fast_mcp_cls(
+            server_name,
+            instructions=instructions,
+            stateless_http=True,
+            json_response=True,
+            streamable_http_path="/",
+            **server_kwargs,
+        )
+
+        def _json_normalize(obj: Any) -> Any:
+            # Round-trip through reflex's JSON encoder so state-native values
+            # (datetimes, enums, ...) become plain JSON before MCP serialises.
+            return json.loads(json_dumps(obj))
+
+        def _resolve_event(event_name: str) -> RegisteredEventHandler:
+            """Resolve an event name to its handler, or raise with suggestions.
+
+            Args:
+                event_name: The name the caller supplied.
+
+            Returns:
+                The registered handler.
+
+            Raises:
+                ValueError: If the event is unknown.
+            """
+            reh = handler_index.get(event_name) or handler_index.get(
+                event_name.replace("/", ".")
+            )
+            if reh is None:
+                suggestions = _suggest_event_names(handler_index, event_name)
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Unknown event {event_name!r}. Use the search_events tool "
+                    "to discover valid event names. "
+                    f"Did you mean: {', '.join(suggestions)}?"
+                )
+            return reh
+
+        # The session tools/resources always derive the caller's session from
+        # the validated bearer token (OAuth or anonymous) -- never from a
+        # caller-supplied token argument. Defined in mcp_auth.tools: the tool
+        # functions need the SDK's ``Context`` importable at module scope for
+        # annotation evaluation.
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.tools import (
+            MCPSessionAccess,
+            register_session_tools,
+        )
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.rate_limit import SlidingWindowRateLimiter
+
+        session_access = MCPSessionAccess(
+            authorization_server=authorization_server,
+            anonymous_issuer=anonymous_issuer,
+            delta_sink=sink,
+            pending_updates_mode=cast(SinkMode, self.pending_updates),
+            rate_limiter=(

+                if self.call_rate_limit > 0

+            ),
+            enforce_auth=self._auth_plugin() is not None,
+        )

+            app,
+            mcp_server,
+            session_access,
+            _resolve_event,
+            _json_normalize,
+            self.path,
+            mcp_upload_url,
+            descriptions=descriptions,
+            max_search_results=self.max_search_results,
+            expose_events=self.expose_events,
+        )
+
+        return mcp_server

+"""State backing the MCP authorization consent page.
+
+The consent page is the single human checkpoint of the MCP OAuth flow: the
+upstream IdP consent screen is routinely skipped for already-authenticated
+browsers, so approval here is what stops a malicious MCP client from silently
+acting as the user (the confused-deputy attack the MCP security best practices
+call out).
+
+Because this state lives in ``reflex_enterprise`` it is framework-exempt:
+its handlers are withheld from the MCP/REST surfaces (agents can never queue
+``approve``) and the per-event ``AuthMiddleware`` gate skips it — so the
+handlers below re-verify the caller's identity themselves via
+``AuthUserState.current()`` instead of trusting the page guard alone.
+
+Approval is always an explicit click: a prior consent is surfaced as a hint
+(``previously_authorized``) but never silently auto-submits at page load. A
+silent on-load auto-approve could not be gated against a framed window, because
+the client-side iframe check fires on mount and has not reported back yet when
+the ``on_load`` handler runs — so the framed-window guard would be a no-op on
+that path. Requiring the click defers the decision until after the check has
+round-tripped.
+
+CSRF/clickjacking posture: the approve/deny events arrive over the app's own
+websocket carrying the browser session's client token, so a cross-site page
+cannot forge them; the transaction id is bound server-side at load time (the
+event payload cannot override it); ``MCPPlugin`` serves the consent path with
+``X-Frame-Options: DENY`` / ``frame-ancestors 'none'`` wherever the backend
+serves the frontend (split-serve deployments must send those headers from the
+frontend host); and as defense-in-depth the explicit approve handler refuses to
+run in an iframed window (``IsIframedState``, reliable by click time).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+from urllib.parse import urlparse
+
+import reflex as rx
+
+# Imported at runtime (not only under TYPE_CHECKING): with
+# ``from __future__ import annotations`` the handlers' ``-> EventSpec | None``
+# return annotations are strings, and reflex's event processor resolves them via
+# ``get_type_hints`` when transforming the payload -- a TYPE_CHECKING-only import
+# would make that raise ``NameError`` and log a warning on every call.
+from reflex.event import EventSpec
+
+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.store import ProviderTokenSnapshot
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.provider import MCPAuthorizationServer
+
+__all__ = ["MCPConsentState"]
+
+_FLOW_RESTART_HINT = (
+    "Restart the authorization from your MCP client to get a fresh request."
+)
+
+
+class MCPConsentState(rx.State):
+    """Loads a pending MCP authorization and records the user's decision.
+
+    The ``load_authorization_request`` / ``approve`` / ``deny`` handlers make a
+    few ``await``ed auth-store calls (cross-process Redis round-trips on a
+    Redis-backed deployment) while holding the Reflex state lock, rather than
+    moving that I/O to an ``rx.background`` task per the usual guidance. This is
+    deliberate: the consent decision must be transactionally consistent -- the
+    approval atomically consumes the pending transaction, records consent, and
+    mints exactly one authorization code, then returns the client redirect as
+    the handler's result -- so it cannot be split across a background task
+    without losing the single-decision guarantee and the redirect response. The
+    operations are few, bounded, and per-user (one interactive click), so the
+    lock is held only briefly; the security and correctness of the OAuth
+    checkpoint take precedence over shaving that latency here.
+    """
+
+    #: Human-readable client name from the (attacker-controlled) registration.
+    client_name: str = ""
+    #: The exact redirect URI the code will be sent to.
+    redirect_uri: str = ""
+    #: The scopes the client requested (excluding the app-defined ones, which
+    #: are shown as individually grantable checkboxes instead).
+    requested_scopes: list[str] = []
+    #: The developer-defined app scopes offered on this consent screen:
+    #: ``[{"name", "description"}, ...]`` (see ``MCPPlugin(app_scopes=...)``).
+    app_scope_options: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+    #: The user's per-app-scope grant decision, keyed by scope name. Seeded
+    #: from the client's request (a requested app scope starts ticked); the
+    #: checkboxes toggle it. Only names in ``app_scope_options`` are honored.
+    app_scope_grants: dict[str, bool] = {}
+    #: Why the request cannot proceed ("" when it can).
+    error_message: str = ""
+    #: True once a valid pending authorization is loaded (enables the buttons).
+    ready: bool = False
+    #: True when the user already approved this exact client + redirect URI with
+    #: at least these scopes — shown as a hint; never used to auto-approve.
+    previously_authorized: bool = False
+
+    #: The transaction under decision; server-only, bound at load time.
+    _txn_id: str = ""
+
+    @rx.var
+    def redirect_host(self) -> str:
+        """The redirect URI's host, displayed alongside the client name.
+
+        ``client_name`` is attacker-controlled text from dynamic client
+        registration (consent phishing), so the page always shows where the
+        authorization code will actually be sent.
+        """
+        if not self.redirect_uri:
+            return ""
+        parsed = urlparse(self.redirect_uri)
+        return parsed.netloc or self.redirect_uri
+
+    @rx.var
+    def has_requested_scopes(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the client requested any scopes (drives the scope list)."""
+        return bool(self.requested_scopes)
+
+    @rx.var
+    def has_app_scopes(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the app defines grantable scopes (drives the checkboxes)."""
+        return bool(self.app_scope_options)
+
+    @rx.event
+    def set_app_scope_grant(self, scope_name: str, granted: bool) -> None:
+        """Record the user ticking/unticking one app scope checkbox.
+
+        Only scope names the app actually defines are recorded — anything else
+        is ignored, so a tampering client cannot smuggle extra scope names
+        into the grant.
+
+        Args:
+            scope_name: The app scope being toggled.
+            granted: The checkbox state.
+        """
+        if any(option["name"] == scope_name for option in self.app_scope_options):
+            self.app_scope_grants[scope_name] = bool(granted)
+
+    def _authorization_server(self) -> MCPAuthorizationServer | None:
+        """Return the bound authorization server, or record an error.
+
+        Returns:
+            The active server, or None (with ``error_message`` set).
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.provider import (
+            get_mcp_authorization_server,
+        )
+
+        server = get_mcp_authorization_server()
+        if server is None:
+            self.error_message = (
+                "MCP authorization is not active on this app. Enable the "
+                "MCPPlugin together with an AuthPlugin."
+            )
+        return server
+
+    async def _current_identity(self) -> tuple[str, ProviderTokenSnapshot] | None:
+        """Resolve the logged-in human's subject and provider-token snapshot.
+
+        Identity comes from this event's own session tree
+        (``AuthUserState.current()`` / ``current_provider()``), never from the
+        client payload.
+
+        Returns:
+            A ``(subject, snapshot)`` pair, or None when the visitor is not
+            fully authenticated (``error_message`` is set).
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.user_state import AuthUserState
+
+        userinfo = await AuthUserState.current()
+        provider_cls = await AuthUserState.current_provider()
+        if not userinfo or provider_cls is None:
+            self.error_message = "You must be signed in to authorize an MCP client."
+            return None
+        subject = userinfo.get("sub", "")
+        if not subject:
+            self.error_message = (
+                "Your identity provider returned no stable subject (sub) claim; "
+                "cannot record consent."
+            )
+            return None
+        provider_state = await self.get_state(provider_cls)
+        snapshot = ProviderTokenSnapshot(
+            provider_name=provider_cls.__provider__,
+            access_token_data=provider_state._access_token_data or "",
+            id_token=provider_state._id_token or "",
+            refresh_token=provider_state._refresh_token or "",
+            granted_scopes=provider_state._granted_scopes or "",
+        )
+        if not snapshot.access_token_data or not snapshot.id_token:
+            self.error_message = (
+                "Your login session holds no usable tokens; sign in again."
+            )
+            return None
+        return subject, snapshot
+
+    async def _is_iframed(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the page reported it is running inside an iframe.
+
+        Returns:
+            True when iframed (or the check reported cross-origin denial).
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.oidc.state import IsIframedState
+
+        return (await self.get_state(IsIframedState)).is_iframed
+
+    @rx.event
+    async def load_authorization_request(self) -> EventSpec | None:
+        """Load the pending authorization named by the ``txn`` query parameter.
+
+        Runs as the page's ``on_load`` (after the ``auth=True`` page guard).
+        When the visitor is authenticated and has previously consented to this
+        exact client + redirect URI with at least these scopes, the approval is
+        short-circuited without re-prompting.
+
+        Returns:
+            A redirect to the client when auto-approval applies, else None.
+        """
+        self.error_message = ""
+        self.ready = False
+        server = self._authorization_server()
+        if server is None:
+            return None
+        txn_id = self.router.url.query_parameters.get("txn", "")
+        if not txn_id:
+            self.error_message = (
+                f"Missing authorization request reference. {_FLOW_RESTART_HINT}"
+            )
+            return None
+        txn = await server.load_pending_authorization(txn_id)
+        if txn is None:
+            self.error_message = (
+                f"This authorization request is unknown or has expired. "
+                f"{_FLOW_RESTART_HINT}"
+            )
+            return None
+        self._txn_id = txn_id
+        self.client_name = txn.client_name or txn.client_id
+        self.redirect_uri = txn.redirect_uri
+        # Developer-defined app scopes are offered as individual checkboxes; a
+        # requested one starts ticked, an unrequested one unticked. The plain
+        # (non-app) requested scopes are listed as before and granted wholesale
+        # on approval.
+        app_scopes = server.config.app_scopes or {}
+        self.app_scope_options = [
+            {"name": name, "description": description}
+            for name, description in app_scopes.items()
+        ]
+        self.app_scope_grants = {name: name in txn.scopes for name in app_scopes}
+        self.requested_scopes = [s for s in txn.scopes if s not in app_scopes]
+        # Whether the user has approved this exact client + redirect URI with at
+        # least these scopes before, shown as a "previously authorized" hint.
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.user_state import AuthUserState
+
+        userinfo = await AuthUserState.current()
+        subject = (userinfo or {}).get("sub", "")
+        self.previously_authorized = bool(
+            subject and await server.has_covering_consent(subject=subject, txn=txn)
+        )
+        self.ready = True
+        # The prompt is always shown and requires an explicit Approve click: we
+        # never silently short-circuit on a prior consent. A returning client
+        # re-prompts, but the alternative -- auto-approving at on_load -- cannot
+        # be safely gated against clickjacking, because the client-side iframe
+        # check (fired on mount) has not reported back yet at on_load time, so
+        # the framed-window guard would be a no-op on the silent path. The
+        # explicit approve() below runs after that check has round-tripped and
+        # is additionally protected by the consent route's anti-framing headers.
+        return None
+
+    @rx.event
+    async def approve(self) -> EventSpec | None:
+        """Approve the pending authorization and redirect with the minted code.
+
+        Returns:
+            The redirect to the client's redirect URI (carrying ``code`` and
+            the client's ``state``), or None when the request cannot proceed
+            (``error_message`` explains why).
+        """
+        self.error_message = ""
+        server = self._authorization_server()
+        if server is None:
+            return None
+        if not self._txn_id:
+            self.error_message = (
+                f"No authorization request is loaded. {_FLOW_RESTART_HINT}"
+            )
+            return None
+        if await self._is_iframed():
+            self.error_message = (
+                "Authorization cannot be approved from an embedded frame. "
+                "Open this page in a top-level window."
+            )
+            return None
+        identity = await self._current_identity()
+        if identity is None:
+            return None
+        subject, snapshot = identity
+        # The final grant: the plain requested scopes, plus exactly the app
+        # scopes the user left ticked (restricted to the defined names — the
+        # setter already filters, and the intersection here re-asserts it).
+        defined = {option["name"] for option in self.app_scope_options}
+        granted_scopes: list[str] | None = None
+        if defined:
+            granted_scopes = list(self.requested_scopes) + sorted(
+                name
+                for name, granted in self.app_scope_grants.items()
+                if granted and name in defined
+            )
+        redirect_url = await server.approve_pending_authorization(
+            self._txn_id,
+            subject=subject,
+            snapshot=snapshot,
+            granted_scopes=granted_scopes,
+        )
+        self._txn_id = ""
+        self.ready = False
+        if redirect_url is None:
+            self.error_message = (
+                f"This authorization request has expired. {_FLOW_RESTART_HINT}"
+            )
+            return None
+        return rx.redirect(redirect_url)
+
+    @rx.event
+    async def deny(self) -> EventSpec | None:
+        """Deny the pending authorization and notify the client.
+
+        Returns:
+            The redirect to the client's redirect URI carrying
+            ``error=access_denied``, or None when no request is loaded.
+        """
+        self.error_message = ""
+        server = self._authorization_server()
+        if server is None:
+            return None
+        if not self._txn_id:
+            self.error_message = (
+                f"No authorization request is loaded. {_FLOW_RESTART_HINT}"
+            )
+            return None
+        redirect_url = await server.deny_pending_authorization(self._txn_id)
+        self._txn_id = ""
+        self.ready = False
+        if redirect_url is None:
+            self.error_message = (
+                f"This authorization request has expired. {_FLOW_RESTART_HINT}"
+            )
+            return None
+        return rx.redirect(redirect_url)

+"""The default MCP authorization consent page.
+
+Rendered at the ``MCPPlugin(consent_path=...)`` route (an ``auth=True`` page,
+so the page guard federates login through the configured ``AuthPlugin``
+providers before the prompt is shown). Replaceable via
+``MCPPlugin(consent_page=...)`` with the same builder contract as the
+``AuthPlugin`` page builders.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import reflex as rx
+
+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.consent_state import MCPConsentState
+
+__all__ = ["default_consent_page"]
+
+
+def _iframe_check_mount() -> Any:
+    """The on-mount event chain that detects an iframed window.
+
+    The approve handler refuses to run when the page reports it is iframed
+    (clickjacking defense-in-depth for deployments where the response-header
+    protection does not apply).
+
+    Returns:
+        The mount event.
+    """
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth.oidc.state import IsIframedState
+
+    return rx.cond(
+        ~IsIframedState.checked_this_session,
+        IsIframedState.check_if_iframed.throttle(100),
+        rx.noop(),
+    )
+
+
+def _app_scope_checkbox(option: Any) -> rx.Component:
+    """Render one grantable app-scope row (checkbox + description).
+
+    Args:
+        option: The ``{"name", "description"}`` mapping for the scope.
+
+    Returns:
+        The checkbox row component.
+    """
+    return rx.hstack(
+        rx.checkbox(
+            checked=MCPConsentState.app_scope_grants.get(option["name"], False),
+            # Class-level handler access is an EventHandler taking the payload
+            # args (the metaclass drops ``self``); pyright sees the raw method.
+            on_change=lambda checked: MCPConsentState.set_app_scope_grant(  # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
+                option["name"], checked
+            ),
+        ),
+        rx.vstack(
+            rx.code(option["name"], size="2"),
+            rx.text(option["description"], size="1", color_scheme="gray"),
+            spacing="0",
+            align="start",
+        ),
+        spacing="2",
+        align="start",
+    )
+
+
+def default_consent_page(**context: Any) -> rx.Component:
+    """Render the default MCP client consent prompt.
+
+    Shows who is asking (the registration's ``client_name`` — untrusted text —
+    always alongside the exact redirect host the code will be sent to), the
+    requested scopes, the individually grantable app-defined scopes, and
+    Approve / Deny actions.
+
+    Args:
+        **context: The page-builder context (``plugin``); unused by the
+            default builder.
+
+    Returns:
+        The consent page component.
+    """
+    return rx.center(
+        rx.card(
+            rx.vstack(
+                rx.heading("Authorize MCP access", size="6"),
+                rx.cond(
+                    MCPConsentState.error_message != "",
+                    rx.callout(
+                        MCPConsentState.error_message,
+                        icon="triangle_alert",
+                        color_scheme="red",
+                        role="alert",
+                        width="100%",
+                    ),
+                ),
+                rx.cond(
+                    MCPConsentState.ready,
+                    rx.vstack(
+                        rx.text(
+                            rx.text.strong(MCPConsentState.client_name),
+                            " is asking to act as you in this app.",
+                        ),
+                        rx.text(
+                            "The authorization code will be sent to ",
+                            rx.code(MCPConsentState.redirect_host),
+                            ".",
+                            size="2",
+                        ),
+                        rx.cond(
+                            MCPConsentState.has_requested_scopes,
+                            rx.vstack(
+                                rx.text("Requested scopes:", size="2", weight="bold"),
+                                rx.foreach(
+                                    MCPConsentState.requested_scopes,
+                                    lambda scope: rx.code(scope, size="2"),
+                                ),
+                                spacing="1",
+                                align="start",
+                            ),
+                            rx.text(
+                                "No specific scopes were requested.",
+                                size="2",
+                                color_scheme="gray",
+                            ),
+                        ),
+                        rx.cond(
+                            MCPConsentState.has_app_scopes,
+                            rx.vstack(
+                                rx.text(
+                                    "Grant this client permission to:",
+                                    size="2",
+                                    weight="bold",
+                                ),
+                                rx.foreach(
+                                    MCPConsentState.app_scope_options,
+                                    _app_scope_checkbox,
+                                ),
+                                rx.text(
+                                    "Only the ticked permissions are granted; "
+                                    "the app can restrict what this client may "
+                                    "do based on them.",
+                                    size="1",
+                                    color_scheme="gray",
+                                ),
+                                spacing="2",
+                                align="start",
+                            ),
+                        ),
+                        rx.cond(
+                            MCPConsentState.previously_authorized,
+                            rx.text(
+                                "You have authorized this client before.",
+                                size="1",
+                                color_scheme="gray",
+                            ),
+                        ),
+                        rx.hstack(
+                            rx.button(
+                                "Approve",
+                                on_click=MCPConsentState.approve,
+                                color_scheme="green",
+                            ),
+                            rx.button(
+                                "Deny",
+                                on_click=MCPConsentState.deny,
+                                variant="outline",
+                                color_scheme="red",
+                            ),
+                            spacing="3",
+                        ),
+                        spacing="4",
+                        align="start",
+                    ),
+                ),
+                spacing="4",
+                align="start",
+            ),
+            max_width="28em",
+            width="100%",
+            on_mount=_iframe_check_mount(),
+        ),
+        min_height="60vh",
+        padding="2em",
+    )
