+"""The MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server + token verifier.
+
+``MCPAuthorizationServer`` implements the ``mcp`` SDK's
+``OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider`` protocol, federating the human
+authentication step to the app's existing ``AuthPlugin`` OIDC flow:
+
+1. ``/authorize`` parks the validated request as a pending transaction and
+   redirects the browser to the consent page — a normal ``auth=True`` Reflex
+   page, so the page guard bounces an anonymous visitor through the standard
+   ``/login`` palette (any configured provider) and back.
+2. The consent approve handler snapshots the authenticated human's provider
+   tokens and mints a single-use authorization code bound to the client's PKCE
+   challenge (client<->facade PKCE is independent of the facade<->IdP PKCE the
+   login flow used).
+3. The token exchange allocates a fresh Reflex client token (``T_mcp``), seeds
+   that session's provider state with the snapshot (server-side; semantically a
+   second browser login), and issues opaque, resource-bound access/refresh
+   tokens of our own. Upstream IdP tokens never reach the MCP client, and
+   upstream refresh keeps happening server-side through the provider state.
+
+Spec MUSTs covered here: no token passthrough in either direction (our opaque
+tokens out; ``verify_token`` only accepts tokens we minted for our resource),
+single-use short-lived codes, refresh rotation, and sessions-are-not-auth (the
+MCP tools derive the session from the validated bearer token — never from a
+caller-supplied token argument).
+
+This module imports the optional ``mcp`` SDK at import time; ``MCPPlugin``
+imports it lazily only after confirming the SDK is installed.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import secrets
+import time
+import uuid
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+from urllib.parse import urlparse
+
+from mcp.server.auth.provider import (
+    AccessToken,
+    AuthorizationCode,
+    AuthorizationParams,
+    AuthorizeError,
+    OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider,
+    RefreshToken,
+    RegistrationError,
+    TokenError,
+    TokenVerifier,
+    construct_redirect_uri,
+)
+from mcp.shared.auth import OAuthClientInformationFull, OAuthToken
+
+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.backend_delta_sink import BackendDeltaSink, SinkMode
+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.store import (
+    ClientConsent,
+    MCPAuthStore,
+    PendingAuthorization,
+    ProviderTokenSnapshot,
+    StoredAccessToken,
+    StoredAuthorizationCode,
+    StoredRefreshToken,
+    StoredUploadTicket,
+    canonical_resource,
+    hash_secret,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from reflex.app import App
+
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth.oidc.state import OIDCAuthState
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth.oidc.types import OIDCUserInfo
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Loopback hosts allowed to use plain-http redirect URIs (RFC 8252 §7.3) —
+# and, matching them, the hosts allowed a plain-http *issuer* in development.
+_LOOPBACK_HOSTS = ("127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost")
+
+__all__ = [
+    "MCPAuthConfig",
+    "MCPAuthorizationServer",
+    "ReflexMCPAccessToken",
+    "ReflexMCPAuthorizationCode",
+    "ReflexMCPRefreshToken",
+    "ReflexMCPTokenVerifier",
+    "bind_mcp_authorization_server",
+    "canonical_resource",
+    "get_mcp_authorization_server",
+]
+
+
+class ReflexMCPAccessToken(AccessToken):
+    """Our access token, carrying the Reflex session it is bound to.
+
+    The extra fields ride on the model only server-side — the SDK never
+    renders provider token models to clients (see the note in
+    ``mcp/server/auth/provider.py``).
+    """
+
+    reflex_client_token: str = ""
+    grant_id: str = ""
+
+
+class ReflexMCPRefreshToken(RefreshToken):
+    """Our refresh token, carrying the Reflex session and grant it belongs to."""
+
+    reflex_client_token: str = ""
+    grant_id: str = ""
+    resource: str | None = None
+
+
+class ReflexMCPAuthorizationCode(AuthorizationCode):
+    """Our authorization code, carrying the provider-token snapshot to seed."""
+
+    snapshot: ProviderTokenSnapshot | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
+class MCPAuthConfig:
+    """Static configuration for the MCP authorization server."""
+
+    #: Public origin serving the OAuth endpoints (RFC 8414 issuer).
+    issuer_url: str
+    #: Absolute URL of the MCP endpoint (the RFC 8707 resource identifier).
+    resource_server_url: str
+    #: Absolute URL of the consent page (the app page users approve on).
+    consent_url: str
+    #: Lifetime of a pending authorization (login + consent window).
+    pending_authorization_ttl: float = 600.0  # 10 minutes
+    #: Lifetime of a minted authorization code (single-use regardless).
+    authorization_code_ttl: float = 60.0  # 1 minute
+    #: Lifetime of an issued access token.
+    access_token_ttl: float = 3600.0  # 1 hour
+    #: Lifetime of an issued refresh token (rotated on each use).
+    refresh_token_ttl: float | None = 30 * 24 * 3600.0  # 30 days
+    #: Lifetime of a dynamic client registration (None = no expiry).
+    client_ttl: float | None = 90 * 24 * 3600.0  # 90 days
+    #: Lifetime of a pre-signed file-upload ticket (short-lived by design).
+    upload_ticket_ttl: float = 300.0  # 5 minutes
+    #: Developer-defined app-specific scopes (name -> human description), each
+    #: individually grantable on the consent screen. The minted tokens carry
+    #: only the scopes the user granted; auth checks read them via
+    #: ``ctx.token_scopes``.
+    app_scopes: dict[str, str] | None = None
+
+
+class MCPAuthorizationServer(
+    OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider[
+        ReflexMCPAuthorizationCode, ReflexMCPRefreshToken, ReflexMCPAccessToken
+    ]
+):
+    """OAuth AS for the MCP endpoint, federating login to the ``AuthPlugin``."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *, app: App, store: MCPAuthStore, config: MCPAuthConfig) -> None:
+        """Initialize the authorization server.
+
+        Args:
+            app: The Reflex app whose sessions the tokens bind to.
+            store: Persistence for clients, txns, codes, tokens and consent.
+            config: Static endpoint/TTL configuration.
+        """
+        self.app = app
+        self.store = store
+        self.config = config
+        self._canonical_resource = canonical_resource(config.resource_server_url)
+        # MCP sessions have no websocket -- their deltas are returned to the
+        # agent via the tool result -- so followup emissions targeting them are
+        # diverted off the socket path through this sink (registered on seed,
+        # dropped or queued per the configured mode; see backend_delta_sink).
+        # None until the plugin attaches one; seeding still works without it
+        # (emissions just log the usual disconnected-client warning).
+        self.delta_sink: BackendDeltaSink | None = None
+        self.pending_updates_mode: SinkMode = "drop"
+
+    def attach_delta_sink(
+        self, sink: BackendDeltaSink, *, mode: SinkMode = "drop"
+    ) -> None:
+        """Attach the backend-delta sink the seeded sessions register with.
+
+        Args:
+            sink: The app-level sink whose guard diverts socket emissions.
+            mode: How followup deltas for MCP sessions are handled --
+                ``"drop"`` discards them, ``"queue"`` buffers them for
+                retrieval via the ``get_pending_updates`` tool.
+        """
+        self.delta_sink = sink
+        self.pending_updates_mode = mode
+
+    def _is_own_resource(self, resource: str | None) -> bool:
+        """Whether ``resource`` identifies this MCP server (RFC 8707 audience).
+
+        Every credential this server issues is bound to
+        :attr:`_canonical_resource`; a record carrying any other resource was
+        minted for a different server (e.g. one sharing the token store) and
+        must not be honored here. A record with no resource is treated as not
+        ours -- issued records always carry one.
+
+        Args:
+            resource: The record's stored resource identifier.
+
+        Returns:
+            True when the resource canonicalizes to this server's resource.
+        """
+        return (
+            resource is not None
+            and canonical_resource(resource) == self._canonical_resource
+        )
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Client registration (RFC 7591 dynamic client registration).
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    async def get_client(self, client_id: str) -> OAuthClientInformationFull | None:
+        """Look up a registered client.
+
+        Args:
+            client_id: The client id issued at registration.
+
+        Returns:
+            The registration record, or None when unknown/expired.
+        """
+        return await self.store.get_client(client_id)
+
+    async def register_client(self, client_info: OAuthClientInformationFull) -> None:
+        """Validate and store a dynamic client registration.
+
+        Redirect URIs must be exact absolute URLs: ``https`` for anything, and
+        plain ``http`` only for RFC 8252 loopback hosts (native apps receiving
+        the code on ``http://127.0.0.1:{port}/...``). Everything else —
+        including custom URL schemes — is rejected.
+
+        Args:
+            client_info: The registration record built by the SDK handler.
+
+        Raises:
+            RegistrationError: When a redirect URI is not acceptable.
+        """
+        for redirect_uri in client_info.redirect_uris or []:
+            parsed = urlparse(str(redirect_uri))
+            if parsed.scheme == "https":
+                continue
+            if parsed.scheme == "http" and parsed.hostname in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS:
+                continue
+            raise RegistrationError(
+                error="invalid_redirect_uri",
+                error_description=(
+                    f"redirect_uri {redirect_uri} must be https, or http on a "
+                    "loopback host (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost)."
+                ),
+            )
+        await self.store.put_client(client_info, ttl=self.config.client_ttl)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Authorization (the federation entry point).
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    async def authorize(
+        self, client: OAuthClientInformationFull, params: AuthorizationParams
+    ) -> str:
+        """Park the request and send the browser to the consent page.
+
+        The SDK handler has already validated the client, the redirect URI
+        (exact match against the registration) and the requested scopes. Here
+        the RFC 8707 ``resource`` is checked against this server's canonical
+        resource, the transaction is persisted with the client's PKCE
+        challenge and ``state``, and the browser is redirected to the consent
+        page — whose ``auth=True`` page guard federates the actual login.
+
+        Args:
+            client: The validated client.
+            params: The validated authorization parameters.
+
+        Returns:
+            The consent-page URL to redirect the browser to.
+
+        Raises:
+            AuthorizeError: When ``resource`` names a different server.
+        """
+        if (
+            params.resource is not None
+            and canonical_resource(params.resource) != self._canonical_resource
+        ):
+            raise AuthorizeError(
+                error="invalid_request",
+                error_description=(
+                    f"resource {params.resource} does not identify this MCP "
+                    f"server (expected {self.config.resource_server_url})."
+                ),
+            )
+        now = time.time()
+        txn = PendingAuthorization(
+            txn_id=secrets.token_urlsafe(32),
+            client_id=str(client.client_id),
+            client_name=client.client_name or "",
+            redirect_uri=str(params.redirect_uri),
+            redirect_uri_provided_explicitly=params.redirect_uri_provided_explicitly,
+            code_challenge=params.code_challenge,
+            scopes=list(params.scopes or []),
+            resource=params.resource,
+            client_state=params.state,
+            created_at=now,
+            expires_at=now + self.config.pending_authorization_ttl,
+        )
+        await self.store.put_pending_authorization(txn)
+        return construct_redirect_uri(self.config.consent_url, txn=txn.txn_id)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Consent-side API (called by the consent page's event handlers).
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    async def load_pending_authorization(
+        self, txn_id: str
+    ) -> PendingAuthorization | None:
+        """Return an unexpired pending authorization, or None.
+
+        Args:
+            txn_id: The transaction id from the consent-page query string.
+
+        Returns:
+            The pending authorization, or None when unknown/expired.
+        """
+        return await self.store.get_pending_authorization(txn_id)
+
+    async def has_covering_consent(
+        self, *, subject: str, txn: PendingAuthorization
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Whether a recorded consent already covers this exact request.
+
+        Auto-approval requires the exact ``(subject, client_id)`` consent to
+        cover the exact ``redirect_uri`` with the requested scopes a subset of
+        those previously granted — scope escalation always re-prompts.
+
+        Args:
+            subject: The authenticated user's stable subject claim.
+            txn: The pending authorization under consideration.
+
+        Returns:
+            True when the consent page may skip the prompt.
+        """
+        consent = await self.store.get_consent(subject, txn.client_id)
+        return consent is not None and consent.covers(txn.redirect_uri, txn.scopes)
+
+    async def approve_pending_authorization(
+        self,
+        txn_id: str,
+        *,
+        subject: str,
+        snapshot: ProviderTokenSnapshot,
+        granted_scopes: list[str] | None = None,
+    ) -> str | None:
+        """Record consent, mint the authorization code, and build the redirect.
+
+        Args:
+            txn_id: The approved transaction.
+            subject: The authenticated user's stable subject claim.
+            snapshot: The user's provider tokens, captured from their session.
+            granted_scopes: The final scopes the user granted on the consent
+                screen (the requested non-app scopes plus the individually
+                ticked ``app_scopes``). ``None`` grants exactly the requested
+                scopes. Every token minted from the code carries these.
+
+        Returns:
+            The client redirect URL carrying ``code`` (and the client's
+            ``state``), or None when the transaction is unknown/expired.
+        """
+        # One decision per transaction: atomically consume it before minting, so
+        # two approvals racing on the same consent prompt (e.g. a double-submit
+        # from two browser contexts) cannot both read it and mint two codes --
+        # only the caller that removes it proceeds.
+        txn = await self.store.consume_pending_authorization(txn_id)
+        if txn is None:
+            return None
+
+        scopes = list(granted_scopes) if granted_scopes is not None else txn.scopes
+        raw_code = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
+        await self.store.put_authorization_code(
+            StoredAuthorizationCode(
+                code_hash=hash_secret(raw_code),
+                client_id=txn.client_id,
+                redirect_uri=txn.redirect_uri,
+                redirect_uri_provided_explicitly=txn.redirect_uri_provided_explicitly,
+                code_challenge=txn.code_challenge,
+                scopes=scopes,
+                # Bind the code to THIS server's resource (the client's
+                # requested resource was already validated to equal it, or was
+                # omitted). Every token minted from it is bound the same way, so
+                # the code is uniformly audience-checkable at redemption.
+                resource=self._canonical_resource,
+                subject=subject,
+                snapshot=snapshot,
+                expires_at=time.time() + self.config.authorization_code_ttl,
+            )
+        )
+        await self._record_consent(subject=subject, txn=txn, scopes=scopes)
+        return construct_redirect_uri(
+            txn.redirect_uri, code=raw_code, state=txn.client_state
+        )
+
+    async def deny_pending_authorization(self, txn_id: str) -> str | None:
+        """Drop the transaction and build the ``access_denied`` redirect.
+
+        Args:
+            txn_id: The denied transaction.
+
+        Returns:
+            The client redirect URL carrying ``error=access_denied`` (and the
+            client's ``state``), or None when the transaction is
+            unknown/expired.
+        """
+        # Consume atomically for the same one-decision-per-transaction property
+        # as approval: a denial and a racing approval cannot both fire.
+        txn = await self.store.consume_pending_authorization(txn_id)
+        if txn is None:
+            return None
+        return construct_redirect_uri(
+            txn.redirect_uri,
+            error="access_denied",
+            error_description="The user denied the authorization request.",
+            state=txn.client_state,
+        )
+
+    async def _record_consent(
+        self,
+        *,
+        subject: str,
+        txn: PendingAuthorization,
+        scopes: list[str] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Merge this approval into the ``(subject, client_id)`` consent record.
+
+        Args:
+            subject: The authenticated user's stable subject claim.
+            txn: The approved transaction.
+            scopes: The scopes actually granted (defaults to the requested
+                ones) — what the record accumulates, so a later request for a
+                scope the user previously *unticked* re-prompts.
+        """
+        existing = await self.store.get_consent(subject, txn.client_id)
+        redirect_uris = set(existing.redirect_uris) if existing else set()
+        recorded_scopes = set(existing.scopes) if existing else set()
+        redirect_uris.add(txn.redirect_uri)
+        recorded_scopes.update(txn.scopes if scopes is None else scopes)
+        await self.store.put_consent(
+            ClientConsent(
+                subject=subject,
+                client_id=txn.client_id,
+                redirect_uris=sorted(redirect_uris),
+                scopes=sorted(recorded_scopes),
+                granted_at=time.time(),
+            )
+        )
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Token endpoint.
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    async def load_authorization_code(
+        self, client: OAuthClientInformationFull, authorization_code: str
+    ) -> ReflexMCPAuthorizationCode | None:
+        """Load a minted code by its presented value.
+
+        The SDK's ``TokenHandler`` then enforces client binding, expiry,
+        redirect-URI equality and the PKCE verifier before calling
+        :meth:`exchange_authorization_code`.
+
+        Args:
+            client: The client presenting the code.
+            authorization_code: The raw code from the token request.
+
+        Returns:
+            The code record, or None when unknown/expired.
+        """
+        record = await self.store.get_authorization_code(
+            hash_secret(authorization_code)
+        )
+        if record is None or not self._is_own_resource(record.resource):
+            # Not ours (e.g. a code minted by a different MCP server sharing the
+            # token store): treat as unknown so it cannot be redeemed here.
+            return None
+        return ReflexMCPAuthorizationCode(
+            code=authorization_code,
+            scopes=record.scopes,
+            expires_at=record.expires_at,
+            client_id=record.client_id,
+            code_challenge=record.code_challenge,
+            redirect_uri=record.redirect_uri,  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
+            redirect_uri_provided_explicitly=record.redirect_uri_provided_explicitly,
+            resource=record.resource,
+            subject=record.subject,
+            snapshot=record.snapshot,
+        )
+
+    async def exchange_authorization_code(
+        self,
+        client: OAuthClientInformationFull,
+        authorization_code: ReflexMCPAuthorizationCode,
+    ) -> OAuthToken:
+        """Consume the code, seed the MCP session, and issue our tokens.
+
+        Args:
+            client: The authenticated client (PKCE already verified by the
+                SDK handler).
+            authorization_code: The loaded code record.
+
+        Returns:
+            The issued (opaque, resource-bound) access + refresh tokens.
+
+        Raises:
+            TokenError: ``invalid_grant`` when the code was already used or the
+                upstream session could not be established.
+        """
+        # Single-use: exactly one of two racing exchanges can consume the code.
+        if not await self.store.consume_authorization_code(
+            hash_secret(authorization_code.code)
+        ):
+            raise TokenError(
+                error="invalid_grant",
+                error_description="authorization code already used or expired",
+            )
+        snapshot = authorization_code.snapshot
+        if snapshot is None:
+            raise TokenError(
+                error="invalid_grant",
+                error_description="authorization code carries no session snapshot",
+            )
+        reflex_client_token = str(uuid.uuid4())
+        if not await self._seed_reflex_session(reflex_client_token, snapshot):
+            raise TokenError(
+                error="invalid_grant",
+                error_description=(
+                    "the upstream login session could not be established; "
+                    "re-run the authorization flow"
+                ),
+            )
+        return await self._mint_grant(
+            client_id=str(client.client_id),
+            scopes=authorization_code.scopes,
+            subject=authorization_code.subject or "",
+            reflex_client_token=reflex_client_token,
+            grant_id=secrets.token_urlsafe(16),
+        )
+
+    async def load_refresh_token(
+        self, client: OAuthClientInformationFull, refresh_token: str
+    ) -> ReflexMCPRefreshToken | None:
+        """Load a refresh token by its presented value.
+
+        Args:
+            client: The client presenting the token.
+            refresh_token: The raw refresh token from the token request.
+
+        Returns:
+            The refresh-token record, or None when unknown/expired.
+        """
+        record = await self.store.get_refresh_token(hash_secret(refresh_token))
+        if record is None or not self._is_own_resource(record.resource):
+            # Audience binding: a refresh token minted for another resource
+            # (e.g. a different MCP server sharing the store) is not ours to
+            # rotate. Mirrors load_access_token so refresh tokens are bound too.
+            return None
+        return ReflexMCPRefreshToken(
+            token=refresh_token,
+            client_id=record.client_id,
+            scopes=record.scopes,
+            expires_at=int(record.expires_at) if record.expires_at else None,
+            subject=record.subject,
+            reflex_client_token=record.reflex_client_token,
+            grant_id=record.grant_id,
+            resource=record.resource,
+        )
+
+    async def exchange_refresh_token(
+        self,
+        client: OAuthClientInformationFull,
+        refresh_token: ReflexMCPRefreshToken,
+        scopes: list[str],
+    ) -> OAuthToken:
+        """Rotate the grant's tokens, re-checking the upstream session.
+
+        Both tokens rotate: the presented refresh token is atomically consumed
+        and the grant's outstanding access token revoked before a new pair is
+        minted for the same Reflex session. If the MCP session no longer
+        resolves a user (upstream refresh failed server-side), the grant dies
+        with ``invalid_grant`` so the client re-runs the authorization flow.
+
+        Args:
+            client: The authenticated client.
+            refresh_token: The loaded refresh-token record.
+            scopes: The (already validated) scopes for the new access token.
+
+        Returns:
+            The freshly minted access + refresh token pair.
+
+        Raises:
+            TokenError: ``invalid_grant`` when the token was already rotated or
+                the upstream session is gone.
+        """
+        consumed = await self.store.consume_refresh_token(
+            hash_secret(refresh_token.token)
+        )
+        if consumed is None:
+            raise TokenError(
+                error="invalid_grant",
+                error_description="refresh token already used or expired",
+            )
+        # The old access token dies with the rotation.
+        await self.store.revoke_grant(consumed.grant_id)
+        userinfo = await self.resolve_session_userinfo(consumed.reflex_client_token)
+        if not userinfo:
+            await self.reset_reflex_session(consumed.reflex_client_token)
+            raise TokenError(
+                error="invalid_grant",
+                error_description=(
+                    "the upstream login session has expired; re-run the "
+                    "authorization flow"
+                ),
+            )
+        return await self._mint_grant(
+            client_id=consumed.client_id,
+            scopes=scopes,
+            subject=consumed.subject,
+            reflex_client_token=consumed.reflex_client_token,
+            grant_id=consumed.grant_id,
+        )
+
+    async def load_access_token(self, token: str) -> ReflexMCPAccessToken | None:
+        """Verify a presented bearer token and return its access record.
+
+        Only tokens this server minted — and minted for this resource — are
+        accepted: upstream IdP tokens (or tokens for another MCP server sharing
+        the store) hash to nothing / fail the resource check.
+
+        Args:
+            token: The raw bearer token.
+
+        Returns:
+            The access-token record, or None when invalid/expired.
+        """
+        record = await self.store.get_access_token(hash_secret(token))
+        if record is None or not self._is_own_resource(record.resource):
+            return None
+        return ReflexMCPAccessToken(
+            token=token,
+            client_id=record.client_id,
+            scopes=record.scopes,
+            expires_at=record.expires_at,
+            resource=record.resource,
+            subject=record.subject,
+            reflex_client_token=record.reflex_client_token,
+            grant_id=record.grant_id,
+        )
+
+    async def create_upload_ticket(
+        self, reflex_client_token: str, event_handler: str
+    ) -> str:
+        """Mint a short-lived pre-signed ticket authorizing an upload to a session.
+
+        Returned in the clear inside the OAuth upload URL so an agent can POST a
+        file upload without presenting (or even knowing) its bearer token. The
+        ticket resolves to this one session **and this one handler**, is bound
+        to this resource server, and expires after ``config.upload_ticket_ttl``.
+
+        Args:
+            reflex_client_token: The session an upload with this ticket applies to.
+            event_handler: The fully-qualified registry name of the handler the
+                ticket authorizes (the upload endpoint rejects a mismatched
+                ``Reflex-Event-Handler``).
+
+        Returns:
+            The raw ticket string to embed in the upload URL.
+        """
+        raw = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
+        await self.store.put_upload_ticket(
+            StoredUploadTicket(
+                token_hash=hash_secret(raw),
+                reflex_client_token=reflex_client_token,
+                resource=self._canonical_resource,
+                expires_at=time.time() + self.config.upload_ticket_ttl,
+                event_handler=event_handler,
+            )
+        )
+        return raw
+
+    async def resolve_upload_ticket(self, ticket: str) -> StoredUploadTicket | None:
+        """Resolve (and consume) a pre-signed upload ticket to its record.
+
+        The ticket is *consumed* on resolution (single-use, like authorization
+        codes): a leaked upload URL cannot be replayed within the ticket's TTL
+        to re-drive the bound handler in the victim's session. Each upload
+        intent mints its own ticket via :meth:`create_upload_ticket`.
+
+        Args:
+            ticket: The raw ticket presented on the upload URL.
+
+        Returns:
+            The stored ticket record (carrying the bound ``reflex_client_token``
+            and ``event_handler``), or None when the ticket is unknown, already
+            used, expired, or minted for another resource server.
+        """
+        record = await self.store.consume_upload_ticket(hash_secret(ticket))
+        if record is None or not self._is_own_resource(record.resource):
+            return None
+        return record
+
+    async def revoke_token(
+        self, token: ReflexMCPAccessToken | ReflexMCPRefreshToken
+    ) -> None:
+        """Revoke the whole grant behind either token, and clear its session.
+
+        Args:
+            token: The access or refresh token presented for revocation.
+        """
+        grant_id = getattr(token, "grant_id", "")
+        reflex_client_token = getattr(token, "reflex_client_token", "")
+        if grant_id:
+            revoked_refresh = await self.store.revoke_grant(grant_id)
+            if not reflex_client_token and revoked_refresh is not None:
+                reflex_client_token = revoked_refresh.reflex_client_token
+        if reflex_client_token:
+            # Don't leave upstream tokens parked in a session nothing can use.
+            await self.reset_reflex_session(reflex_client_token)
+
+    async def revoke_grant_and_session(
+        self, *, grant_id: str, reflex_client_token: str
+    ) -> None:
+        """Revoke a grant's tokens and reset its MCP session.
+
+        Used by the MCP tools when a call finds the upstream session dead: the
+        agent then gets a clean 401 on its next request and re-runs the flow.
+
+        Args:
+            grant_id: The grant to revoke.
+            reflex_client_token: The Reflex session to clear.
+        """
+        await self.store.revoke_grant(grant_id)
+        await self.reset_reflex_session(reflex_client_token)
+
+    async def _mint_grant(
+        self,
+        *,
+        client_id: str,
+        scopes: list[str],
+        subject: str,
+        reflex_client_token: str,
+        grant_id: str,
+    ) -> OAuthToken:
+        """Mint and store an access + refresh token pair for a grant.
+
+        Args:
+            client_id: The client the tokens are issued to.
+            scopes: The granted scopes.
+            subject: The resource owner's subject claim.
+            reflex_client_token: The Reflex session the tokens address.
+            grant_id: The grant identifier tying the pair together.
+
+        Returns:
+            The RFC 6749 token response payload.
+        """
+        raw_access = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
+        raw_refresh = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
+        now = int(time.time())
+        access_expires_at = now + int(self.config.access_token_ttl)
+        refresh_expires_at = (
+            now + int(self.config.refresh_token_ttl)
+            if self.config.refresh_token_ttl is not None
+            else None
+        )
+        await self.store.put_access_token(
+            StoredAccessToken(
+                token_hash=hash_secret(raw_access),
+                client_id=client_id,
+                scopes=scopes,
+                resource=self._canonical_resource,
+                subject=subject,
+                reflex_client_token=reflex_client_token,
+                grant_id=grant_id,
+                expires_at=access_expires_at,
+            )
+        )
+        await self.store.put_refresh_token(
+            StoredRefreshToken(
+                token_hash=hash_secret(raw_refresh),
+                client_id=client_id,
+                scopes=scopes,
+                resource=self._canonical_resource,
+                subject=subject,
+                reflex_client_token=reflex_client_token,
+                grant_id=grant_id,
+                expires_at=refresh_expires_at,
+            )
+        )
+        return OAuthToken(
+            access_token=raw_access,
+            token_type="Bearer",
+            expires_in=int(self.config.access_token_ttl),
+            scope=" ".join(scopes) if scopes else None,
+            refresh_token=raw_refresh,
+        )
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Reflex session bridging.
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _provider_class(self, provider_name: str) -> type[OIDCAuthState] | None:
+        """Resolve a ``__provider__`` name to a configured provider class.
+
+        Args:
+            provider_name: The recorded ``__provider__`` string.
+
+        Returns:
+            The provider class, or None when it is no longer configured.
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement import get_auth_providers
+
+        for provider in get_auth_providers():
+            if provider.__provider__ == provider_name:
+                return provider
+        return None
+
+    def _state_token(self, reflex_client_token: str) -> Any:
+        """Build the root ``BaseStateToken`` for a Reflex client token.
+
+        Args:
+            reflex_client_token: The session's client token.
+
+        Returns:
+            The ``BaseStateToken`` addressing the session's root state.
+        """
+        from reflex.istate.manager.token import BaseStateToken
+        from reflex.state import State
+
+        return BaseStateToken(ident=reflex_client_token, cls=State)
+
+    async def _seed_reflex_session(
+        self, reflex_client_token: str, snapshot: ProviderTokenSnapshot
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Seed a fresh MCP session's provider state with the snapshot tokens.
+
+        Replays the exact writes a browser login performs: ``_set_tokens``
+        (which re-validates the id_token and resets the session on failure)
+        and ``_populate_auth_user_state``. After this, the entire enforcement
+        stack — the per-event gate, ``resolve_userinfo``, delta filtering,
+        ``AuthUserState.current()`` — works on the MCP session unchanged, and
+        upstream token refresh happens server-side through the provider state.
+
+        Args:
+            reflex_client_token: The freshly allocated session token (T_mcp).
+            snapshot: The provider tokens captured at consent time.
+
+        Returns:
+            True when the session now holds a valid, resolvable login.
+        """
+        provider_cls = self._provider_class(snapshot.provider_name)
+        if provider_cls is None:
+            logger.error(
+                "MCP token exchange: provider %r from the consent snapshot is "
+                "not configured; cannot seed the session.",
+                snapshot.provider_name,
+            )
+            return False
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.event_handler_api import router_data_for_token
+
+        try:
+            async with self.app.modify_state(
+                self._state_token(reflex_client_token)
+            ) as root:
+                # Give the session a non-empty router_data so the event
+                # processor treats it as already-hydrated: its "rehydrate on an
+                # empty router" compatibility hack would otherwise re-run the
+                # page's hydrate + on_load chain (enforce_login, data loaders)
+                # on every agent tool call. The agent never loads a page; its
+                # delta comes from the tool result. Persists in the in-memory
+                # state manager (the Redis manager drops router_data on
+                # serialize, so re-run there is avoided only for the in-process
+                # case -- acceptable, since those deltas are dropped anyway).
+                root.router_data = router_data_for_token(reflex_client_token)
+                # Also refresh the ``router`` var, not just ``router_data`` (as
+                # ``persist_router_data`` does -- we can't call it here without
+                # nesting a second ``modify_state``). Headless state reads on this
+                # OAuth session authorize via ``_access_for_state``, which reads
+                # the session client token off ``router.session``; an empty
+                # ``router`` var resolves to the browser surface and would bypass
+                # scope-aware ``auth=`` checks. Unlike ``router_data`` (which the
+                # Redis manager drops on serialize), the ``router`` var persists.
+                from reflex.istate.data import RouterData
+
+                root.router = RouterData.from_router_data(root.router_data)
+                provider_state = await root.get_state(provider_cls)
+                await provider_state._set_tokens(
+                    access_token=snapshot.access_token_data,
+                    id_token=snapshot.id_token or None,
+                    refresh_token=snapshot.refresh_token or None,
+                    granted_scopes=snapshot.granted_scopes or None,
+                )
+                if not await provider_state._validate_tokens():
+                    # _set_tokens already reset the session on failure.
+                    return False
+                await provider_state._populate_auth_user_state(
+                    clear_previous_provider=True
+                )
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception(
+                "MCP token exchange: failed to seed the Reflex session with the "
+                "provider tokens."
+            )
+            return False
+        else:
+            if self.delta_sink is not None:
+                self.delta_sink.register(
+                    reflex_client_token, mode=self.pending_updates_mode
+                )
+            return True
+
+    async def resolve_session_userinfo(
+        self, reflex_client_token: str
+    ) -> OIDCUserInfo | None:
+        """Resolve the userinfo for an MCP session (refreshing upstream if due).
+
+        Runs the same ``resolve_userinfo`` the per-event gate uses, inside a
+        ``modify_state`` block so a server-side upstream token refresh is
+        persisted.
+
+        Args:
+            reflex_client_token: The MCP session's client token.
+
+        Returns:
+            The resolved userinfo, or None when the session has no valid login.
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement import resolve_userinfo
+
+        try:
+            async with self.app.modify_state(
+                self._state_token(reflex_client_token)
+            ) as root:
+                return await resolve_userinfo(root)
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("MCP auth: failed to resolve session userinfo.")
+            return None
+
+    async def reset_reflex_session(self, reflex_client_token: str) -> None:
+        """Clear an MCP session's provider tokens and protected app state.
+
+        Args:
+            reflex_client_token: The MCP session's client token.
+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement import get_auth_providers
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.user_state import AuthUserState
+
+        try:
+            async with self.app.modify_state(
+                self._state_token(reflex_client_token)
+            ) as root:
+                auth_user = await root.get_state(AuthUserState)
+                provider_cls = auth_user.provider
+                if provider_cls is None:
+                    for provider in get_auth_providers():
+                        provider_state = await root.get_state(provider)
+                        if (
+                            provider_state._access_token_data
+                            or provider_state._id_token
+                            or provider_state._refresh_token
+                        ):
+                            provider_cls = provider
+                            break
+                if provider_cls is not None:
+                    provider_state = await root.get_state(provider_cls)
+                    await provider_state._reset_session()
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("MCP auth: failed to reset the MCP session state.")
+        finally:
+            if self.delta_sink is not None:
+                self.delta_sink.unregister(reflex_client_token)
+            # Forget the session's recorded access surface/scopes: nothing can
+            # drive it anymore, and a stale entry must not describe a future
+            # session that happens to reuse the token string.
+            from reflex_enterprise.auth.access import clear_api_access
+
+            clear_api_access(reflex_client_token)
+
+
+class ReflexMCPTokenVerifier(TokenVerifier):
+    """The resource-server-side bearer check FastMCP gates the transport with.
+

+"""Persistence for the MCP OAuth authorization server.
+
+Stores the records the OAuth facade needs across requests (and, with Redis,
+across workers): registered clients, pending authorization transactions,
+authorization codes, access/refresh tokens, and per-user per-client consent.
+
+Secret handling:
+
+- The **lookup secrets** we mint -- authorization codes and access/refresh
+  token strings -- are stored **hashed** (SHA-256) and only ever matched by
+  hash. They are high-entropy random strings, so the hash is a pure one-way
+  index: the stored hash cannot be replayed as a credential against this
+  server, and lookup stays O(1).
+- Client records are stored **verbatim**, including ``client_secret``. This is
+  required by the ``mcp`` SDK: its ``ClientAuthenticator`` compares the
+  presented secret against ``client.client_secret`` with
+  ``hmac.compare_digest`` (``mcp/server/auth/middleware/client_auth.py``), so
+  ``get_client`` must return the raw secret. The secret is itself a random
+  server-generated credential scoped to one registration.
+- The authorization-code record carries a :class:`ProviderTokenSnapshot` -- the
+  consenting user's **upstream** provider tokens -- in the clear, for the code's
+  brief single-use lifetime (``authorization_code_ttl``, 60s by default), so the
+  token exchange can seed the MCP session. These are the same upstream tokens
+  the ``AuthPlugin`` already persists (unencrypted) in the reflex state store
+  for every logged-in session, so this adds no at-rest exposure beyond that
+  store; it is *not* covered by the one-way-hash property above. Protect the
+  backing store (Redis ACLs/encryption-at-rest) as you would the session store.
+
+Single-use semantics (auth codes, refresh-token rotation) are enforced with
+atomic consume operations so two concurrent exchanges can never both succeed.
+The in-memory backend also evicts expired records opportunistically on write so
+abandoned pre-consent transactions cannot accumulate unboundedly; the Redis
+backend relies on server-side key TTLs.

+    """Return the storage hash for a code/token secret.

+    Args:
+        secret: The raw secret presented by (or issued to) a client.
+
+    Returns:

+    """
+    return hashlib.sha256(secret.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

+def canonical_resource(url: str) -> str:
+    """Canonicalize a resource identifier for RFC 8707 comparison.
+
+    Applies the MCP authorization spec's canonicalization: lowercase the scheme
+    and host, drop a default port (``:80`` for http, ``:443`` for https), and
+    strip a trailing slash from the path (path case is preserved). So
+    ``https://App.example:443/MCP/`` and ``https://app.example/MCP`` compare
+    equal, while ``/MCP`` and ``/mcp`` stay distinct.
+
+    Lives here (not in ``provider``) so the anonymous-token issuer can use it
+    without the optional ``mcp`` SDK installed — this module imports the SDK
+    only lazily.
+
+    Args:
+        url: The resource URL to canonicalize.
+
+    Returns:
+        The canonical form used for equality comparison.
+    """
+    parsed = urlparse(url)
+    scheme = parsed.scheme.lower()
+    host = (parsed.hostname or "").lower()
+    netloc = host
+    # Keep a non-default port; drop the scheme's default port.
+    if parsed.port is not None and str(parsed.port) != _DEFAULT_PORTS.get(scheme):

+"""The bearer-token-bound MCP tools.
+
+Lives in its own module (imported only after ``MCPPlugin`` confirmed the
+optional ``mcp`` SDK is installed) so ``Context`` is importable at module
+scope: FastMCP evaluates the tools' string type annotations against this
+module's globals to discover the injected context parameter.
+
+Sessions are not authentication: these tools never accept a caller-supplied
+``token``. The Reflex session is derived from the validated bearer token's
+``reflex_client_token`` binding — an OAuth token minted by the authorization
+server (whose upstream login is pre-flighted on every call, performing the
+server-side token refresh, so an expired session surfaces as a clear
+re-authenticate error instead of an empty delta) or an anonymous session token
+from the token-granting endpoint (no identity, no preflight). Every call is
+rate limited per session token, and the session's access surface + token
+scopes are recorded for the auth checks (``ctx.surface`` /
+``ctx.token_scopes``).
+"""
+

+
+import dataclasses
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated, Any, Callable
+
+from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context
+from pydantic import Field

+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.api_tokens import ANONYMOUS_CLIENT_ID
+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.event_handler_api import (
+    apply_event_collect_delta,
+    canonical_event_name,
+    full_event_handler_name,
+    router_data_for_token,
+    sanitize_agent_delta,
+    upload_handler_kind,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from reflex.app import App
+    from reflex_base.registry import RegisteredEventHandler
+
+    from reflex_enterprise.plugins.api_tokens import AnonymousSessionIssuer
+    from reflex_enterprise.plugins.backend_delta_sink import BackendDeltaSink, SinkMode
+    from reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.provider import MCPAuthorizationServer
+    from reflex_enterprise.plugins.rate_limit import SlidingWindowRateLimiter
+

+
+_REAUTH_HINT = (
+    "Re-run the OAuth authorization flow (discovered via the MCP server's "
+    "WWW-Authenticate / protected-resource metadata) to establish a new session."
+)
+
+_NO_SESSION_HINT = (
+    "No authenticated MCP session is attached to this request. Present an "
+    "app-issued bearer token: run the OAuth authorization flow, or request an "
+    "anonymous session token from the app's token endpoint "
+    "(POST /_reflex/auth/token)."

+def _access_token_from_context(ctx: Context | None) -> Any | None:
+    """Read the request's validated access token.
+
+    Prefers the ``AuthContextMiddleware`` contextvar; falls back to the
+    authenticated user the ASGI AuthenticationMiddleware attached to the
+    request scope (robust even if the contextvar does not propagate into the
+    tool task).
+
+    Args:
+        ctx: The FastMCP request context, when available.
+
+    Returns:
+        The ``AccessToken`` for this request, or None.
+    """
+    from mcp.server.auth.middleware.auth_context import get_access_token
+
+    access_token = get_access_token()
+    if access_token is not None:
+        return access_token
+    if ctx is None:
+        return None
+    try:
+        request = ctx.request_context.request
+    except (LookupError, ValueError):
+        return None
+    user = getattr(request, "user", None)
+    return getattr(user, "access_token", None)

+    """Session resolution + per-call policy shared by the MCP tools/resources.
+
+    Wraps the plugin's token authorities: the OAuth authorization server (when
+    MCP OAuth is on) and/or the anonymous session issuer (when the token
+    endpoint is on). ``require_session`` is the single chokepoint every
+    session-touching tool and resource goes through — it resolves the caller's
+    session from the validated bearer, pre-flights an OAuth session's upstream
+    login, applies the per-token rate limit, and records the access surface +
+    scopes for the enforcement layer.

+    anonymous_issuer: AnonymousSessionIssuer | None

+    #: active) — used to fail anonymous calls on auth-required handlers with a
+    #: clear error instead of a blocked-event redirect delta.

+
+        Args:
+            ctx: The FastMCP request context.

+            The validated ``(access_token, reflex_client_token)`` pair.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: When no authenticated MCP session is attached.
+        """
+        access_token = _access_token_from_context(ctx)
+        reflex_client_token = getattr(access_token, "reflex_client_token", "") or (
+            (getattr(access_token, "claims", None) or {}).get("reflex_client_token", "")
+        )
+        if not access_token or not reflex_client_token:
+            raise ValueError(_NO_SESSION_HINT)
+        return access_token, reflex_client_token

+
+        Args:
+            reflex_client_token: The session the call is billed to.

+        """
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.rate_limit import check_call_rate

+                f"{max(int(retry_after), 1)} second(s)."

+        fail when an upstream login has lapsed) the way ``require_session`` does.

+        Args:
+            ctx: The FastMCP request context.
+
+        Returns:

+
+        Raises:

+    async def require_session(self, ctx: Context | None, handler: Any = None) -> str:

+        Args:

+            handler: The event handler about to be dispatched (for per-handler

+
+        Returns:

+
+        Raises:

+        """
+        access_token, reflex_client_token = self._resolve_token(ctx)

+        # trigger a server-side token refresh (network I/O), which is exactly
+        # the kind of per-call cost the limiter must bound.
+        self._enforce_rate_limit(reflex_client_token, handler)

+            userinfo = await self.authorization_server.resolve_session_userinfo(
+                reflex_client_token

+            if not userinfo:

+                await self.authorization_server.revoke_grant_and_session(

+        import time as _time
+
+        from reflex_enterprise.auth.access import ApiAccessInfo, record_api_access

+        expires_at = getattr(access_token, "expires_at", None)
+        record_api_access(

+            ApiAccessInfo(

+                grant_id=getattr(access_token, "grant_id", "") or "",

+"""The built-in ``reflex://`` resource family: state + event introspection.
+
+Registered on the FastMCP server. Two groups:
+
+* **Metadata** (session-independent, snapshotted at build time):
+  ``reflex://state`` (exposed state names) and -- when the plugin exposes
+  events -- ``reflex://event`` / ``reflex://event/{event_name}`` (handler
+  enumeration + detail) and ``reflex://state/events/{state_name}`` (a state's
+  handlers).
+* **Session state** (read live per request): ``reflex://state/vars/{state_name}``
+  -- the resolved ``.dict()`` rooted at a state (cached var values) -- and
+  ``reflex://state/vars/{state_name}/{var_name}`` -- a single var's live value
+  (a computed var is marked dirty and recomputed). The session is always the
+  one bound to the caller's validated bearer token (resolved through
+  ``require_session``, which also applies the per-token rate limit); there is
+  no caller-supplied token.
+
+The ``search_events`` tool is unaffected: it stays the server-side filtered
+entry point for large apps, while these resources support flat enumeration.
+
+Imported only after ``MCPPlugin`` has confirmed the optional ``mcp`` SDK is
+installed (like the sibling ``mcp_auth.tools`` module), so ``Context`` is
+importable at module scope.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import inspect
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Callable
+
+from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context
+
+from reflex_enterprise.plugins.event_handler_api import (
+    describe_event_handler,
+    iter_public_event_handlers,
+    resolve_state_dict,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from reflex.app import App
+    from reflex_base.registry import RegisteredEventHandler
+
+__all__ = ["register_reflex_resources"]
+

+def _exposed_state_names() -> list[str]:
+    """Return the fully-qualified names of the app's exposed states.
+
+    The root ``State`` (the whole-app read) plus every non-exempt state -- the
+    app's own states, excluding the framework/auth states hidden from the agent
+    surface. Snapshotted at build time (the registration context is live then).
+
+    Returns:
+        Sorted fully-qualified state names.
+    """
+    from reflex.state import State
+    from reflex_base.registry import RegistrationContext
+
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement import is_exempt
+
+    names = {State.get_full_name()}
+    # Snapshot the registry: resolving ``is_exempt`` / ``get_full_name`` below
+    # can lazily materialize a substate and register it into ``base_states``,
+    # which would otherwise raise "dictionary changed size during iteration".
+    for state_cls in list(RegistrationContext.get().base_states.values()):
+        if not is_exempt(state_cls):
+            names.add(state_cls.get_full_name())
+    return sorted(names)

+    app: App,
+    mcp_server: Any,
+    resolve_event: Callable[[str], RegisteredEventHandler],

+    rate_limit: Callable[..., Any],

+
+    Args:
+        app: The reflex app.
+        token: The client token identifying the session.
+        state_name: The fully-qualified state name owning the var.
+        var_name: The frontend or computed var name.
+        enforce_auth: Whether to resolve the user + apply protection (OAuth mode).
+        allowed_states: The fully-qualified names of the states exposed on the
+            agent surface (``reflex://state``), snapshotted at build. A state not
+            in this set -- notably a framework/auth state hidden as exempt -- is
+            treated as unknown, so its vars cannot be read by naming it directly
+            here (the whole-state ``.dict()`` path already drops exempt states).
+
+    Returns:
+        A dict with ``state``, ``var``, ``computed`` and the resolved ``value``.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the state/var is unknown or the var is withheld.
+    """
+    import reflex.state as _rx_state
+    from reflex.istate.manager.token import BaseStateToken
+    from reflex.state import State
+    from reflex_base.constants.state import FIELD_MARKER
+
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth import enforcement
+
+    with app.set_contexts():
+        root = await app.state_manager.get_state(BaseStateToken(ident=token, cls=State))
+        # Gate on the exposed-state allowlist before resolving anything: an
+        # exempt (framework/auth) state is not on the surface and must read as
+        # unknown -- never leak that it exists, and never read its vars.
+        if state_name not in allowed_states:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unknown state {state_name!r}. Use a fully-qualified state name "
+                "from `reflex://state`."
+            )
+        try:
+            state_cls = State.get_class_substate(state_name)
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unknown state {state_name!r}. Use a fully-qualified state name "
+                "from `reflex://state`."
+            ) from None
+        substate = await root.get_state(state_cls)
+
+        computed = state_cls.computed_vars.get(var_name)
+        is_computed = computed is not None
+        if is_computed:
+            # Recompute from scratch rather than serve a cached value.
+            computed.mark_dirty(instance=substate)
+            value = getattr(substate, var_name)
+            if inspect.iscoroutine(value):
+                value = await value
+        elif var_name in state_cls.base_vars:
+            value = getattr(substate, var_name)
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{var_name!r} is not a frontend or computed var on {state_name!r}. "
+                "Backend (server-only) vars are not exposed; read "
+                f"`reflex://state/vars/{state_name}` to list the readable vars."
+            )
+
+        if enforce_auth:
+            # Load + sync the session's AuthUserState into the tree so the
+            # protection filter (which reads identity from the tree, not an
+            # ambient contextvar) can authorize the value.
+            await enforcement.resolve_userinfo(root)
+        # Route the value through the same protection filter as ``.dict()`` so a
+        # withheld var is dropped/placeholdered here too (inert without an
+        # AuthPlugin -- the state is then not swept). ``defer_to_guard`` resolves
+        # an async check inline via a guard coroutine ``_resolve_delta`` awaits.
+        full_name = substate.get_full_name()
+        marked = var_name + FIELD_MARKER
+        filtered = await _rx_state._resolve_delta(
+            enforcement.filter_protected_delta(
+                substate, {full_name: {marked: value}}, defer_to_guard=True
+            )
+        )
+
+    resolved = filtered.get(full_name, {})
+    if marked not in resolved:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{var_name!r} on {state_name!r} is not accessible for the current "
+            "session (it is protected and the session is not authorized for it)."
+        )
+    # Redact the server-side session identifiers if the caller read the router
+    # var directly (its ``session.client_token`` must never reach the client).
+    value_out = resolved[marked]
+    if var_name == "router":
+        from reflex_enterprise.plugins.event_handler_api import redact_router_session
+
+        holder = redact_router_session({full_name: {marked: value_out}})
+        value_out = holder[full_name][marked]
+    return {
+        "state": state_name,
+        "var": var_name,
+        "computed": is_computed,
+        "value": value_out,
+    }

+"""Serve ``rxe.mcp.resource`` methods as FastMCP resource templates.
+
+For each decorated State method this builds a resource whose URI-template
+variables are the method's parameters, resolves the caller's session from the
+validated bearer token (``require_session``, which also applies the per-token
+rate limit), enforces the method's ``auth=`` when an ``AuthPlugin`` provides
+identity, calls the method **read-only** on the session's state instance, and
+returns the value. These are resources, not event handlers -- ``queue_event``
+is unaffected.
+
+Imported only after ``MCPPlugin`` has confirmed the optional ``mcp`` SDK is
+installed (like :mod:`reflex_enterprise.plugins.mcp_auth.tools`), so ``Context``
+is importable at module scope.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import inspect
+import logging
+import typing
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Callable
+
+from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context
+
+from reflex_enterprise.mcp import (
+    MCPResourceSpec,
+    iter_state_resources,
+    resource_parameter_names,
+    resource_uri_template,
+    short_state_name,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from reflex.app import App
+
+__all__ = [
+    "register_state_resources",
+]
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def register_state_resources(
+    app: App,
+    mcp_server: Any,
+    require_session: Callable[..., Any],
+    json_normalize: Callable[[Any], Any],
+    *,
+    enforce_auth: bool = True,
+) -> None:
+    """Register the ``rxe.mcp.resource`` methods on the server.
+
+    The session is derived from the validated bearer token (via
+    ``require_session``) and each resource's ``auth=`` is enforced when an
+    ``AuthPlugin`` provides identity.
+
+    Args:
+        app: The reflex app the resources read from.
+        mcp_server: The ``FastMCP`` server to register on.
+        require_session: The tools' session resolver -- ``await
+            require_session(ctx)`` returns the caller's Reflex client token
+            (raising to re-authenticate when the session is gone, and applying
+            the per-token rate limit).
+        json_normalize: Normalises a return value through reflex's JSON encoder.
+        enforce_auth: Whether each resource's ``auth=`` is enforced (an
+            ``AuthPlugin`` is configured). Without one there is no identity
+            system and the whole app is ungated, so resources follow suit.
+    """
+    for state_cls, method_name, fn, spec in iter_state_resources():
+        param_names = resource_parameter_names(fn)
+        uri = resource_uri_template(state_cls, method_name, param_names)
+        wrapper = _build_resource_wrapper(
+            app,
+            state_cls,
+            method_name,
+            fn,
+            spec,
+            param_names,
+            json_normalize,
+            require_session=require_session,
+            enforce_auth=enforce_auth,
+        )
+        mcp_server.resource(
+            uri,
+            name=spec.name or f"{short_state_name(state_cls)}.{method_name}",
+            description=spec.description or _docstring_summary(fn),
+            mime_type=spec.mime_type or "application/json",
+        )(wrapper)
+
+
+def _docstring_summary(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> str | None:
+    """Return the first line of a function's docstring, if any.
+
+    Args:
+        fn: The function to read.
+
+    Returns:
+        The summary line, or None.
+    """
+    doc = inspect.getdoc(fn)
+    return doc.splitlines()[0].strip() if doc else None
+
+
+# Name of the parameter the generated wrapper appends for FastMCP to fill with
+# the request ``Context``. Deliberately not ``ctx`` (a plausible URI-variable
+# name a resource method might legitimately use) so the two never collide; the
+# SDK matches the context parameter by TYPE, not name, so any non-underscore
+# identifier works, and a method parameter that happens to reuse this name is
+# rejected below with a clear error.
+_INJECTED_CONTEXT_PARAM = "rxe_request_context"
+
+
+def _build_resource_wrapper(
+    app: App,
+    state_cls: type,
+    method_name: str,
+    fn: Callable[..., Any],
+    spec: MCPResourceSpec,
+    param_names: list[str],
+    json_normalize: Callable[[Any], Any],
+    *,
+    require_session: Callable[..., Any],
+    enforce_auth: bool,
+) -> Callable[..., Any]:
+    """Build the FastMCP callable for one resource method.
+
+    The wrapper needs an exact signature (its parameters must line up with the
+    URI-template variables, and FastMCP introspects it to build the input
+    schema and to spot the injected ``Context``). The method itself takes
+    ``self``, so a delegating wrapper is generated with the right signature and
+    the implementation runs the method against the resolved session state.
+
+    Args:
+        app: The reflex app the resource reads from.
+        state_cls: The state class owning the method.
+        method_name: The resource method name.
+        fn: The resource method (unbound).
+        spec: The resource's resolved configuration.
+        param_names: The method's parameter names (URI-template variables).
+        json_normalize: Normalises the return value through reflex's JSON encoder.
+        require_session: The session resolver (bearer -> client token).
+        enforce_auth: Whether the resource's ``auth=`` is enforced.
+
+    Returns:
+        An async callable with the resource's exact signature.
+    """
+    from reflex.istate.manager.token import BaseStateToken
+    from reflex.state import State
+
+    try:
+        hints = typing.get_type_hints(fn)
+    except Exception:
+        hints = {}
+    method_params = inspect.signature(fn).parameters
+
+    if _INJECTED_CONTEXT_PARAM in param_names:
+        from reflex.utils.exceptions import ConfigError
+
+        raise ConfigError(
+            f"`{state_cls.__name__}.{method_name}` declares a resource parameter "
+            f"named `{_INJECTED_CONTEXT_PARAM}`, which is reserved -- the MCP "
+            "resource wrapper appends a parameter of that name to receive the "
+            "request context. Rename the parameter."
+        )
+
+    async def impl(ctx: Context | None, params: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
+        token = await require_session(ctx)
+
+        with app.set_contexts():
+            root = await app.state_manager.get_state(
+                BaseStateToken(ident=token, cls=State)
+            )
+            substate = await root.get_state(state_cls)
+            if enforce_auth:
+                await _enforce_resource_auth(root, spec, method_name)
+            result = getattr(substate, method_name)(**params)
+            if inspect.iscoroutine(result):
+                result = await result
+        return json_normalize(result)
+
+    # Ordered (name, annotation, has_default, default) for the wrapper's params.
+    param_specs: list[tuple[str, Any, bool, Any]] = []
+    for name in param_names:
+        param = method_params[name]
+        annotation = hints.get(name, str)
+        has_default = param.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty
+        param_specs.append((name, annotation, has_default, param.default))
+
+    # FastMCP resolves a resource by URI: a URI with a ``{var}`` is a template
+    # (matched by regex, ``Context`` injectable), one without is a concrete
+    # resource (looked up by exact URI, whose fn is called with NO arguments --
+    # so no ``Context``). A no-parameter resource therefore has no place for an
+    # injected ``ctx``; its wrapper takes no args and the session is resolved
+    # from the request's access-token contextvar (the same fallback
+    # ``require_session`` already uses when ``ctx`` is absent).
+    inject_ctx = bool(param_names)
+    wrapper = _make_signature_wrapper(param_specs, impl, inject_ctx=inject_ctx)
+    wrapper.__name__ = f"{short_state_name(state_cls).replace('.', '_')}_{method_name}"
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def _make_signature_wrapper(
+    param_specs: list[tuple[str, Any, bool, Any]],
+    impl: Callable[..., Any],
+    *,
+    inject_ctx: bool,
+) -> Callable[..., Any]:
+    """Generate an async function with an exact signature delegating to ``impl``.
+
+    FastMCP introspects the callable via ``inspect.signature(fn, eval_str=True)``
+    and ``typing.get_type_hints`` and wraps it in pydantic's ``validate_call``,
+    so the callable must be a *real* function with genuine parameters and
+    annotations (a faked ``__signature__`` over ``*args`` would disagree with
+    pydantic). It is generated so ``inspect``, ``get_type_hints`` and
+    ``validate_call`` all see the same thing. The generated body collects its
+    parameters into a dict and awaits ``impl(ctx_or_None, params)``.
+
+    Args:
+        param_specs: Ordered ``(name, annotation, has_default, default)`` tuples
+            for the path-variable parameters.
+        impl: The async implementation ``impl(ctx, params_dict)``.
+        inject_ctx: Whether to append a ``Context = None`` parameter (named
+            :data:`_INJECTED_CONTEXT_PARAM`) which FastMCP fills with the request
+            context.
+
+    Returns:
+        The generated async wrapper.
+    """
+    namespace: dict[str, Any] = {"_impl": impl}
+    declarations: list[str] = []
+    for name, annotation, has_default, default in param_specs:
+        namespace[f"_ann_{name}"] = annotation
+        if has_default:
+            namespace[f"_def_{name}"] = default
+            declarations.append(f"{name}: _ann_{name} = _def_{name}")
+        else:
+            declarations.append(f"{name}: _ann_{name}")
+    if inject_ctx:
+        namespace["_Context"] = Context
+        declarations.append(f"{_INJECTED_CONTEXT_PARAM}: _Context = None")
+
+    names = [name for name, *_ in param_specs]
+    collected = ", ".join(f"{name!r}: {name}" for name in names)
+    ctx_arg = _INJECTED_CONTEXT_PARAM if inject_ctx else "None"
+    source = (
+        f"async def _resource({', '.join(declarations)}):\n"
+        f"    return await _impl({ctx_arg}, {{{collected}}})\n"
+    )
+    # ``dont_inherit=True`` keeps this module's ``from __future__ import
+    # annotations`` from leaking into the generated function: with PEP 563 in
+    # effect its parameter annotations would be strings (``"_ann_name"``) that
+    # FastMCP's ``get_type_hints`` could not resolve. Compiled eagerly, the
+    # annotations are the real type objects placed in ``namespace``.
+    code = compile(source, "<rxe-mcp-resource>", "exec", dont_inherit=True)
+    # Controlled, non-user source (built from validated identifiers above).
+    exec(code, namespace)
+    return namespace["_resource"]
+
+
+async def _enforce_resource_auth(
+    root: Any, spec: MCPResourceSpec, method_name: str
+) -> None:
+    """Enforce a resource's ``auth=`` against the session's user (OAuth mode).
+
+    Mirrors the var/event decision tree (:mod:`reflex_enterprise.auth.enforcement`):
+    ``False`` is public; otherwise a user must be resolved; ``True`` allows any
+    authenticated user; a callable receives a ``VarAuthContext`` (var-like -- no
+    concrete ``Var``) and must return truthy. Fails closed (raises) on a missing
+    user, a falsey result, or a raising check.
+
+    Args:
+        root: The root state instance for the caller's session.
+        spec: The resource's resolved configuration.
+        method_name: The resource method name (for error messages).
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the caller is not authorized to read the resource.
+    """
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth import enforcement
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth.types import _UNSET, VarAuthContext
+
+    auth = spec.auth if spec.auth is not _UNSET else enforcement.get_default_auth()
+    if auth is False:
+        return
+
+    userinfo = await enforcement.resolve_userinfo(root)
+    if userinfo is None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Reading the {method_name!r} resource requires an authenticated "
+            "session, but no user could be resolved."
+        )
+    if auth is True:
+        return
+    if not callable(auth):
+        # Malformed ``auth`` (neither bool nor callable): fail closed.
+        raise ValueError(f"Not authorized to read the {method_name!r} resource.")
+
+    from reflex_enterprise.auth.user_state import AuthUserState
+
+    try:
+        auth_user = await root.get_state(AuthUserState)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.error(
+            "Could not load AuthUserState for an MCP resource check; denying.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Not authorized to read the {method_name!r} resource."
+        ) from None
+
+    # Resolve the access surface + token scopes for this session so a
+    # scope-aware check (``ctx.token_scopes is None or "x" in ctx.token_scopes``)
+    # is enforced on MCP resource reads too. Without this the context defaults to
+    # ``surface="browser"`` / ``token_scopes=None`` and a scoped token reads as a
+    # full browser session, bypassing the check.
+    surface, token_scopes = enforcement._access_for_state(auth_user)
+    ctx = VarAuthContext(
+        auth_user_state=auth_user,
+        field_or_var=None,
+        surface=surface,
+        token_scopes=token_scopes,
+    )
+    try:
+        result = auth(ctx)
+        if inspect.isawaitable(result):
+            result = await result
+        allowed = bool(result)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.error(
+            f"Auth check {auth!r} for the {method_name!r} MCP resource raised; "
+            "denying.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        allowed = False
+    if not allowed:
+        raise ValueError(f"Not authorized to read the {method_name!r} resource.")
